Directory tags are shared across the Knowledge domain and reused by multiple directories and articles. See Directory tags.

docs.title: Knowledge workflow
docs.text: The Knowledge domain typically follows this lifecycle:

docs.title: 1. Structure setup
docs.text: Directories and directory tags are defined in Management.

docs.title: 2. Content creation
docs.text: Articles are created and assigned to directories, optionally tagged and enriched with attachments.

docs.title: 3. Publishing
docs.text: Articles are published and become visible in the Knowledge base according to their status and validity settings.

docs.title: 4. Usage
docs.text: Users browse, search, read, and comment on articles in the Knowledge base.

docs.title: 5. Maintenance
docs.text: Content is updated, disabled, or archived as processes and documentation evolve.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
The Knowledge base serves as the central documentation hub of the system. It ensures that:

  • Internal knowledge is structured and accessible
  • Procedures and guidelines are easy to find
  • Documentation is maintained in a controlled and centralized way
  • Employees have a single source of truth for internal instructions

It complements operational domains by supporting them with clear, accessible documentation.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Knowledge base – browse published documentation
  • Directories – manage containers and navigation
  • Articles – author and maintain content
  • Directory tags – define tags for filtering
  • Table of contents – configure directory navigation

docs.title: Knowledge base
docs.text:
The Knowledge base is the main screen where all published Knowledge content is presented. It provides users with a central place to browse, search, and read internal documentation such as instructions, guidelines, procedures, and reference articles.

The Knowledge base is primarily used as an internal documentation library and supports day-to-day operational work across multiple domains.

To access this screen, go to Knowledge / Knowledge base in the navigation.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Knowledge base home page is designed to help users quickly find relevant content. It combines search, tag-based filtering, and visual navigation to surface commonly used or important articles.

The screen is read-only, except for comments on articles where commenting is enabled.

docs.title: Search and filters
docs.text:
At the top of the page, a search bar allows users to search the Knowledge base by:

  • Article title
  • Article content
  • Tags

Below the search bar, tags are displayed and can be used as quick filters. Clicking a tag filters the visible content to articles associated with that tag.

Tags are defined in Directory tags.

docs.title: Popular topics
docs.text:
The Popular topics section groups frequently accessed or highlighted articles by tag.

Each card represents a tag (for example Assembly, Quality, Instructions) and contains a list of related articles. Clicking an article opens it directly.

This section helps users quickly access commonly used instructions and guidelines without browsing the full directory structure.

docs.title: Browse all topics
docs.text:
The Browse all topics section provides a visual overview of Knowledge content, typically represented by directories or curated topics.

Each tile leads to a group of related articles, allowing users to explore the Knowledge base by topic rather than by tag or search.

This is useful for on-boarding, training, and general exploration of available documentation.

Clicking a directory tile opens the directory view, where users can navigate articles and open the table of contents.

docs.title: Directory view
docs.text:
Clicking a directory from Browse all topics opens the directory view, which displays the articles available inside that directory.

The directory view includes:

  • Search bar – searches within the Knowledge base
  • Tag chips – filter content by tags
  • Popular topics – quick access to articles grouped by tag

In the directory view, the menu provides options to: - Edit tags and - Edit the directory.

docs.title: Table of contents
docs.text:
To browse all articles in the directory, open the table of contents using the menu icon in the top-left corner.

The table of contents shows the directory structure and available articles. Clicking an article opens it in the article view.

The directory structure and table of contents are configured in Directories and Table of contents.

docs.title: Article view
docs.text:
Clicking an article opens the article view, where the full content is displayed.

The article view includes:

  • Article title
  • Author
  • Publication date
  • Tags associated with the article
  • Main content (formatted text, lists, instructions)
  • Attachments (if included)
  • Comments section (if enabled)

docs.title: Comments
docs.text:
If commenting is enabled for an article, users can:

  • Add comments
  • Upload files as part of a comment
  • Review comments from other users

Comments can be removed by clicking Delete.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
The Knowledge base is typically used for:

  • Reading work instructions and procedures
  • Accessing internal guidelines and policies
  • Supporting production, logistics, quality, and maintenance activities
  • Onboarding new employees
  • Sharing internal know-how and best practices

Note

  • The Knowledge base displays only published and enabled content.
  • Visibility of articles depends on directory status and publication settings.
  • Commenting and attachments depend on how the article was configured.

docs.title: Articles
docs.text:
Articles are the main content units of the Knowledge base. They contain written documentation such as instructions, guidelines, procedures, and reference information.

Articles belong to a directory and can be organized and navigated using the directory’s table of contents.

To manage articles, go to Knowledge / Management / Directories in the navigation and click Articles under the desired directory (see Directories).

docs.title: Schema
docs.text: Field Description Title Display title of the article (mandatory). Key Short unique identifier for the article (mandatory). Content Main article text edited using the text editor. Attachments Optional files attached to the article. Tags Tags used to categorize and filter the article. Publish date Date from which the article becomes visible. Expiration date Date after which the article is no longer visible. Collaboration Enables or disables comments on the article. Auto save Automatically saves changes while editing.

docs.title: Articles list
docs.text:
The list view displays all articles belonging to the selected directory.

Each row shows: - Article title - Last modified date

Articles can be searched using the Search field in the top-right corner.

Clicking an article opens it for editing.

docs.title: Actions
docs.text: Click the action button to create a new article.

docs.title: Add a new article
docs.text:
When creating or editing an article, the fields described in the Schema section above are available.

While editing an article, click View in the top-left corner to preview how the article will appear in the Knowledge base.

Changes are saved automatically when Auto save is enabled.

docs.title: Text editor
docs.text:
The article content is written using a built-in text editor.

The editor provides common formatting features found in most text editors, including:

  • Text formatting (headings, bold, italics, lists)
  • Text alignment
  • Links and images
  • Fullscreen editing

The editor is designed to support clear, structured documentation without requiring technical knowledge.

docs.title: Attachments
docs.text:
Articles can include file attachments such as documents or images.

Attachments are uploaded using the drop zone in the article edit screen and are displayed with the article content in the Knowledge base.

docs.title: Tags
docs.text:
Tags are used to categorize articles and make them easier to find in the system.

Tags are selected from Directory tags and can be reused across multiple articles.

docs.title: Publish and schedule articles
docs.text:
Articles can be scheduled using:

  • Publish date – defines when the article becomes visible
  • Expiration date – defines when the article is no longer visible

If no dates are set, the article is visible immediately and indefinitely.

docs.title: Collaboration
docs.text:
When Collaboration is enabled, users can add comments to the article.

This allows feedback, clarification, and discussion directly on the documentation.

docs.title: Delete an article
docs.text:
Click Delete on the article edit screen to open a confirmation dialog:

Are you sure you want to delete this record?

If confirmed, the article is permanently removed.

Note

Deleting an article also removes it from the directory’s table of contents.

docs.title: Directories
docs.text:
The Directories code list defines the main content containers used in the Knowledge base. Each directory represents a topic or category (for example Table Assembly, Safety Guidelines, Quality Inspections) and contains articles and a table of contents structure.

Directories are used to organize Knowledge content and determine how articles are grouped and navigated in the Knowledge base.

To access this screen, go to Knowledge / Management / Directories in the navigation.

docs.title: Schema
docs.text: Field Description Name Display name of the directory (mandatory). Key Short unique identifier for the directory (mandatory). Description Optional description explaining the directory’s purpose. Image Optional image used to visually represent the directory (recommended ratio 1:1). Enabled Indicates whether the directory is visible and available in the Knowledge base.

docs.title: Directories list
docs.text:
The list view displays all configured directories.

Each row shows: - Directory – directory name - Links to manage: - Table of contents - Articles

A status indicator appears to the left of each directory name: - Blue – enabled/active directory - Gray – disabled/inactive directory

Directories can be searched using the Search field in the top-right corner.

Clicking a directory name opens it for editing.

docs.title: Add a new directory
docs.text:
Click the action button to add a new directory. Fill in the following fields:

  • Name
  • Key
  • Description (optional)
  • Image (optional)
  • Enabled – controls whether the directory is visible in the Knowledge base

Click Add to save the new directory.

Once created, the directory becomes available in the Knowledge base and can be populated with content.

docs.title: Manage the directory content
docs.text:
After a directory is created, additional configuration options become available directly from the list:

  • Articles – manage articles that belong to the directory
  • Table of contents – define the navigation structure inside the directory

These options are accessed via the links shown below each directory in the list.

Note

Directories define structure only. Articles and table of contents are managed separately.

docs.title: Edit a directory
docs.text:
Click a directory name to open its edit screen.

From the edit screen you can: - Modify directory metadata (name, key, description) - Enable or disable the directory - Update the directory image

Click Save to confirm changes.

docs.title: Delete a directory
docs.text:
Click Delete on the edit screen to open a confirmation dialog:

Are you sure you want to delete this record?

If confirmed, the directory is permanently removed.

Note

A directory can be deleted only if it does not contain articles or table of contents entries.

docs.title: Directory tags
docs.text:
The Directory tags code list defines tags that can be assigned to Knowledge articles. Tags help categorize content and improve searching and filtering within the Knowledge base.

Directory tags are shared across the Knowledge domain and can be reused by multiple directories and articles.

To access this screen, go to Knowledge / Management / Directory tags in the navigation.

docs.title: Schema
docs.text: Field Description Tag Name of the directory tag (mandatory).

docs.title: Directory tags list
docs.text:
The list view displays all configured directory tags.

Each row shows: - Tag – tag name used to classify Knowledge articles

You can use the Search bar to quickly filter tags by name.

Clicking a tag opens it for editing.

docs.title: Actions
docs.text: Select a directory from the left panel, then click the action button to add a new directory tag.

docs.title: Add new directory tag
docs.text:
Enter the required Tag name.

Click Add to save the new tag.

The tag becomes immediately available for use in Knowledge articles.

docs.title: Edit a directory tag
docs.text:
Click a directory tag in the list to open its edit screen.

From the edit screen you can:

  • Modify the tag name
  • Review articles that currently use this tag (read-only list)

The Articles section helps you understand where the tag is used before making changes or deleting it.

Click Save to confirm changes, or Cancel to discard them and return to the list.

docs.title: Delete a directory tag
docs.text:
Click Delete on the edit screen to open a confirmation dialog:

Are you sure you want to delete this record?

If confirmed, the tag is permanently removed; otherwise, the system keeps it unchanged.

docs.title: Table of contents
docs.text:
The Table of contents defines the navigation structure inside a directory in the Knowledge base. It allows directories to organize articles hierarchically and provides users with a clear way to browse content.

A directory can contain one or more tables of contents. Each table of contents is displayed as a tree and can include folders, article links, and URLs.

To manage the table of contents, go to Knowledge / Management / Directories in the navigation and click Table of contents under the desired directory. See Directories.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The table of contents is displayed as a tree structure and can contain:

  • Folders – used to group entries
  • Articles – links to Knowledge articles
  • URLs – links to external resources

Entries are ordered using an ordinal value.

Tip

Reordering entries is done via the Ordinal field. Drag-and-drop is not supported.

docs.title: Schema
docs.text: Field Description Type Defines the entry type: Folder, Article, or URL. Title Display title of the table of contents entry. Article Article linked to the entry (available when Type = Article). Hyperlink Displayed hyperlink text for URL entries. Ordinal Position of the entry within its level of the table of contents. Enabled For the main table of contents only: controls whether the table of contents is visible in the Knowledge base. Show unused Shows articles not yet used in the table of contents when selecting an article. Synchronize title Keeps the entry title synchronized with the linked article title.

docs.title: Create a table of contents
docs.text:
If a directory does not yet have any table of contents, the screen appears empty.

To create a new table of contents, click the folder icon.

A directory can contain multiple tables of contents. To create a new table of contents (root), make sure you are not focused on an existing table of contents in the sidebar, then click the folder icon.

docs.title: Create a table of contents entry
docs.text:
To add entries, first select the target table of contents in the sidebar, then click the file icon to add a new entry.

When creating an entry, select the desired Type and fill in the relevant fields.

Click Add to create the entry.

docs.title: Edit entries
docs.text:
Click an existing folder or entry in the tree to open its edit screen.

From the edit screen you can:

  • Change the title
  • Update the ordinal
  • Change the linked article or URL, depending on the type
  • For Article entries, the title can optionally be synchronized with the article title.

If a folder is selected in the tree, new entries created will be added inside that folder, allowing you to build a nested table of contents structure.

docs.title: Ordering and hierarchy
docs.text:
• Entries are displayed according to their ordinal value
  • Folders can contain other folders or entries
  • The hierarchy defines how users navigate content in the Knowledge base

Changes to the table of contents are reflected immediately in the selected directory.

Note

The table of contents controls navigation only. Article content is managed separately in Articles.

docs.title: Delete a table of contents or entry
docs.text:
Click Delete on a table of contents or entry to open a confirmation dialog:

Are you sure you want to delete this record?

If confirmed, the table of contents or entry is permanently removed.

docs.title: Using the table of contents in the Knowledge base
docs.text:
Once configured, the table of contents is used when browsing a directory in the Knowledge base.

Inside a directory, click the hamburger icon to open the table of contents panel. This panel allows users to navigate between folders and articles defined in the table of contents.

docs.title: Logistics
docs.text:
The Logistics domain covers all warehouse-related operations within your organization. It includes stock handling processes, warehouse structures, material movements, and all documentation needed to track the physical flow of goods.

Where the Materials domain defines what exists in stock, the Logistics domain defines where it is stored, how it moves, and how it is controlled.

To access this domain, navigate to Logistics in the navigation.

Note

The available domains depend on each company’s configuration and business model.

docs.title: What is included in the Logistics domain?
docs.text:
The domain is organized into several functional areas:

  • Dashboard – high-level overview of warehouse activity (read-only KPIs)
  • Stock – provides a real-time overview of warehouse stock (read-only; filters by warehouse, location, material, batch/serial)
  • Documents – all stock-affecting logistics transactions
  • Views – analytical screens for consumption, issuing, and stock distribution
  • Management – code lists and configuration for warehouses and locations

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text:
The Dashboard provides a high-level overview of logistics performance and warehouse activity. It presents operational indicators (for example, inbound/outbound counts, open inventories, discrepancies) that help users understand current workload, stock movements, and active warehouse processes.

The dashboard serves as the entry point for warehouse supervisors and operators who need immediate insight into the state of logistics operations.

docs.title: Stock
docs.text: The Stock section provides operational insight into warehouse materials and their current quantities. It offers a detailed overview of all materials stored across warehouses and locations. It displays available quantities, batches, serials, and physical positions. This view is read-only.

docs.title: Documents
docs.text:
The Documents section contains all logistics-related transactions that change stock quantities or track warehouse activity.

Available logistics documents include:

  • Receives – Register goods entering the warehouse (procurement, production outputs, customer returns). Increases stock.
  • Simple receive – A lightweight alternative for quick inbound registrations.
  • Issues – Register goods leaving the warehouse (consumption, delivery, production input). Decreases stock.
  • Inter warehouse – Transfer goods between distinct warehouses or sites.
  • Move serial – Relocate serial-numbered or batch materials across locations (does not change quantity).
  • Inventories – Perform stock counts and reconcile discrepancies.
  • Writeoffs – Adjust stock for damaged, lost, or expired materials. Decreases stock.
  • Loans – Track materials temporarily issued to personnel or external partners.
  • Consumptions – Record material consumption events. Decreases stock.
  • Productions – Receive finished or semi-finished goods from production. Increases stock.
  • Reversals – Reverse previous logistics documents and restore prior stock state.
  • Containers – Manage logistics containers, pallets, or grouped items.
  • Disassemblies – Break down products into components returned to stock. Increases component stock.
  • Corrections – Manual corrections of stock records (restricted permissions; audit trail).
  • Move container – Relocate containerized goods as units.
  • Material analysis – Perform diagnostics or quality checks on materials.

Each of these documents contributes to the traceability and accuracy of warehouse operations.

docs.title: Views
docs.text:
The Views section provides analytical tools for understanding stock movements, consumption patterns, and location-based distribution.

Available views include:

  • Consumption details – Insight into material consumption trends and usage patterns; filter by date, material, warehouse, user, cost center.
  • Issue details – Breakdown of issue transactions by material, document, warehouse, location, or user; shows quantities and totals.
  • Stock view by location – Hierarchical representation of stock quantities by warehouse, zone, location (and containers where applicable); includes available vs reserved quantities.

These screens do not create transactions—they are analytical tools meant to support operational decisions.

docs.title: Management
docs.text:
The Management section contains configuration and master data required by all logistics processes.

Available code lists and configuration screens:

  • Configuration – Logistics-wide settings and process behavior.
  • Business directory – Defines internal and external business entities related to logistics.
  • Warehouses – Definitions of physical warehouses or distribution sites.
  • Countries – Geographic data supporting warehouse and partner records.
  • Locations – Storage positions inside warehouses (aisles, racks, bins).
  • Stock boundaries – Logical constraints and special handling rules (for example, quarantine, temperature) for selected materials or locations.
  • Measure units – Unified measurement units used across logistics documents.
  • Material analysis setup – Configuration supporting material inspection or validation processes.

These elements define how logistics operations behave and how data is structured.

Tip

See all management entries in the Management Index.

docs.title: Logistics Processes
docs.text: Logistics operations follow a consistent lifecycle:

docs.title: 1. Receiving goods
docs.text: • Goods enter the warehouse through receives or production outputs.

docs.title: 2. Moving and organizing
docs.text: • Goods are stored, relocated, or distributed across warehouses using inter warehouse, move serial, move container, and locations.

docs.title: 3. Issuing and consuming
docs.text: • Stock leaves the warehouse for production, sales, or internal use via issues and consumptions.

docs.title: 4. Inventory and reconciliation
docs.text: • Accuracy is maintained through inventories, writeoffs, and corrections.

docs.title: 5. Reporting and analysis
docs.text: • Views provide insight into stock usage, availability, and discrepancies (see Views).

docs.title: Logistics and Other Domains
docs.text:
Logistics integrates tightly with other operational areas:

Area Interaction Materials Defines materials stored and moved in logistics. Assets Sales visibility and availability calculations rely on logistics stock. Production Issues and receives connect logistics with production orders. Maintenance Spare parts and maintenance stock flow through logistics. Sales / Supply Logistics ensures availability and correct warehouse fulfillment.

docs.title: Consumptions
docs.text:
A Consumption document records materials that were consumed during the execution of a Production order. Consumption documents are created automatically from the Execution module when a production worker records material consumption. They reduce stock for the consumed materials and provide traceability of what was used.

For the production-side entry of consumed materials, see Consumed — the two are closely linked: recording consumed material in production creates the corresponding consumption document in logistics.

To access this page, go to Logistics / Documents / Consumptions in the navigation.

docs.title: Schema
docs.text: Document Field Description Code Unique identifier of the consumption document (system-generated). Created Timestamp when the document was created. Warehouse Warehouse where the consumed materials were taken from. Details Field Description Material Consumed material (product, semi product, raw material, or repro material). Source Source identifier of the consumed item (for example, a serial number or packaging code, depending on the material tracking method). Quantity Consumed quantity recorded for the material line.

docs.title: List of consumption documents
docs.text:
The Consumptions page displays all consumption documents created through production execution. You can filter the list using:

  • Document dates
  • View
  • Draft — consumption in progress (still being recorded in execution)
  • Committed — finalized consumption document
  • Author
  • Warehouse

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
Consumption documents are not created manually from this page (there is no action button). They are created from the Execution module while recording consumption for a production order. See Consumed for the production entry that triggers these documents.

Workflow notes: - When a production worker starts recording consumption, a Draft consumption document is created automatically. - When the Execution process is completed, the document moves to Committed and can be reviewed in the committed list.

docs.title: Review a consumption document
docs.text: A consumption document contains:

docs.title: Linked documents
docs.text: If the consumption was recorded for a production order, the Linked documents section shows a link to the related Production order (if available).

docs.title: Document and Details
docs.text: The Details section lists all consumed materials with their source and recorded quantities.

docs.title: Delete a consumption document
docs.text: Consumption documents cannot be deleted from the system to ensure traceability of material usage in production, but they can be reversed as described above.

docs.title: Menu
docs.text:
The menu provides additional actions available on this page.

Available actions:

  • Create a new reversal

For details about menu actions, see Menu actions.

docs.title: Containers
docs.text:
A container groups one or more items under a single serial code (often an SSCC – Serial Shipping Container Code). This lets you pack, move, and scan a whole set at once without opening it. Items placed in a container are reserved to that container and cannot be used in other transactions until the container is dissolved or items are removed.

Tip

For a full demonstration, see the Containers video tutorial.

To access this page, go to Logistics / Documents / Containers in the navigation.

docs.title: Schema
docs.text: Document Field Description Code Unique SSCC container identifier (a system‑generated code with this structure: CTR‑YYYY‑NNNNNNNN). Warehouse Warehouse where the container resides. Document date Date the container document was created. Location Warehouse location (for example, Rack/Shelf). Details Field Description Material Packed item (product, semi product, raw or repro material). Serial number Serial/lot identifier of the packed item. Best before Expiration date if tracked. Warehouse location Per‑line location if applicable. Quantity (pc) Quantity of the packed line.

docs.title: List of container documents
docs.text: The Containers page shows all container documents. Use filters such as: - Document dates - View (Open, Packaged) - Warehouse - Author

docs.title: Create a container
docs.text:
Containers are created manually from this page.

  1. Click the action button to create a new container document.

  2. Specify the Warehouse and Location.

  3. The draft container is created. Edit the Document date if needed.

  4. Type or scan a serial number, EAN, or material name into the Details bar. The system displays all matching materials and serial numbers. If multiple items are found, make sure to select the correct one.

  5. Select the right quantity and click Save to save the detail. Repeat with other details if needed.

  6. When ready, click Package to reserve the content and make it ready for logistics operations.

The packaged container is now ready, and the status changes to Packaged. You can use the menu to print or export labels with the container SSCC code.

Note

Items in a Packaged container are reserved and cannot be freely transacted individually. However, the system allows partial quantity usage directly from the container without unpacking it.

docs.title: Using containers
docs.text:
• Picking/issuing: scan the container code during Issues to:
    • add all content at once
    • select and use a partial quantity
  • Receiving/put‑away: scan on Receives to place the full set into stock
  • Moves: use Inter warehouse or Move serial and scan the container to move all items together
  • Stock checks: use Stock / Stock view by location to verify container presence and position

docs.title: Review a container
docs.text:
• Header shows container code, warehouse, date, and location
  • Details list packed items, serials, storage location, and quantities
  • Document Connections (if applicable) show related logistics transactions

Tip

  • Click on the Location link to open the Stock view by location filtered to show only items in that location.
  • Click on a material's serial number to open the Stock view by serial number.

docs.title: Partial quantity usage
docs.text:
A partial quantity can be used from a packaged container without unpacking it.

  • The container remains packaged
  • The remaining quantity stays in the container
  • Only the used quantity is deducted

The system records the container, quantity, document, date, and user.

Supported in Issues, Moves, and Production consumption.

docs.title: Delete a container
docs.text:
• Draft container documents can be deleted freely from the edit screen, using the Delete button. After confirmation, the document is removed from the system without affecting inventory.
  • Packaged containers cannot be deleted; use Dissolve to release contents.

docs.title: Menu
docs.text:
The menu provides additional actions available on this page.

Available actions:

  • Printing — prints the container (SSCC) label
  • Export to PDF — exports the container (SSCC) label as a PDF file

For details about menu actions, see Menu actions.

docs.title: Corrections
docs.text:
Corrections are logistics documents used to adjust inventory when physical stock does not match system records (for example, counting differences, wrong material, or labeling errors). Publishing a correction updates warehouse balances to reflect the actual quantities and properties of materials.

Use Corrections to: - Increase or decrease on-hand quantity for specific serials or items - Update attributes like best-before dates when mislabeled - Fix location discrepancies after physical counts

Note

Corrections affect inventory on publish: the system updates stock levels and attributes based on the entered differences.

To access Corrections, go to Logistics / Documents / Corrections in the navigation.

docs.title: Schema
docs.text:
Document Field Description Code Auto-generated document identifier. Warehouse Warehouse where the correction applies (mandatory). Document date Date of the correction document. Details

Each detail describes the material and the correction to apply.

Field Description Material type Item category, for example, Products, Semi products, Raw materials, Repro materials. Material Selected item (for example, Pine table) from the Assets catalog. Serial number Serial number to which the correction applies, if the material is serialized. Best before Best-before date, if applicable for perishable materials. Warehouse location Bin/shelf in the warehouse for precise placement. See Locations. Quantity Quantity to correct (enter the final quantity or a delta, depending on configuration).

docs.title: List of correction documents
docs.text: The list shows existing Correction documents, with filters for date, warehouse, and status (Draft/Published). Use search to find by code or material.

docs.title: Create a correction document
docs.text:
Create a Correction when the counted stock differs from system stock.

  1. Go to Logistics / Documents / Corrections.

  2. Use the action button to create a draft Correction.

  3. Fill the Document section.

  4. Add items into the details section. Type or scan a serial number, EAN, or material name into the Details bar.

  5. The system displays all matching materials and serial numbers. If multiple matches exist, select the correct one from the list.
  6. Edit the details section, change the Material. Serial number or Quantity as required.

  1. Click Save the confirm added details. Repeat step 4 to add more items.

  2. Click Publish to apply the corrections.

Publishing the correction updates inventory to reflect the new quantities and attributes. The correction document moves to the Committed view.

Important

On publish, inventory is adjusted: quantities increase/decrease to match the correction, and serial/location attributes are updated accordingly.

docs.title: Edit a correction document
docs.text:
1. Click the document Code to open it.
  2. In Draft status, modify header and details as needed.
  3. Use Save to confirm changes.

docs.title: Delete a correction document
docs.text:
• Draft correction documents can be deleted freely from the edit screen, using the Delete button. After confirmation, the document is removed from the system without affecting inventory.
  • Published corrections cannot be deleted.

docs.title: Disassemblies
docs.text:
Disassemblies are logistics documents used to break down a set (combined material) into its individual components. They provide traceability, update stock correctly, and make the parts available for further use in production, supply, or sales.

Use a Disassembly when you receive or store sets (bundled materials) but need to consume or sell their components separately. Publishing a Disassembly reduces the set’s stock and increases the stock of its parts according to the structure defined on the set.

Tip

For a full demonstration, see the Disassemblies video tutorial.

Note

  • Disassembly affects inventory on publish: parts become available and the set quantity decreases accordingly.
  • In order to create a disassembly, we need to first define a set structure in the Sets code list.

To access Disassemblies, go to Logistics / Documents / Disassemblies in the navigation.

docs.title: Example scenario
docs.text: You receive furniture sets, for example a dining set (one table and four chairs) packaged as a single set. To use or sell the items individually, create a Disassembly for the dining set and publish it. The set quantity decreases, and the component parts (table and chairs) appear in stock, ready for picking.

docs.title: Schema
docs.text: Document Field Description Code Auto-generated document code. Document date Date of the disassembly document. Warehouse Warehouse where disassembly occurs (mandatory). Details List of sets to be disassembled (mandatory). Details Field Description Set (material) The combined material (for example, a furniture set) you are disassembling (required). Quantity How many sets to disassemble (required). Serial number Item serial number, if applicable. Best before Best before date for perishable sets/components, if applicable. Warehouse location Bin/shelf used during disassembly or where parts are placed. See Locations.

docs.title: List of disassembly documents
docs.text: The Disassemblies list shows existing documents with status indicators (Draft/Published). A search bar and filters help locate records by warehouse, date, or code.

docs.title: Create a disassembly document
docs.text:
Create a Disassembly to split sets into their parts.

  1. Go to Logistics / Documents / Disassemblies.

  2. Use the action button to create a draft Disassembly.

  3. Fill the Document section.

  4. Add items into the details section. Type or scan a serial number, EAN, or material name into the Details bar.

  5. The system displays all matching materials and serial numbers. If multiple matches exist, select the correct one from the list.

  • Enter the Quantity of sets to disassemble.

  • Click Save the confirm added details. Repeat step 4 to add more items.

  • After saving a detail, click the arrow to expand and see the list of parts that will be disassembled, with their calculated quantities.

  1. Click Publish to commit the disassembly. The document is available for review in the committed list.

Important

On publish, stock is updated: the set disappears (decreases by the disassembled quantity) and parts become available (increase according to the set structure). Locations are respected if provided.

docs.title: Alternative creation path (from Receives)
docs.text:
If you already published a Receive, you can create a disassembly directly from it: - Open the committed Receive. - Use Document connections → + Disassemble.

This creates a Disassembly draft prefilled from the received packages, useful to record disassemblies directly at receipt.

docs.title: Edit a disassembly document
docs.text:
1. Click a document Code to open it.
  2. In Draft status, you can modify header fields and details.
  3. Use Save to confirm changes.

docs.title: Delete a disassembly document
docs.text:
• Draft disassemblies can be deleted freely from the edit screen, using the Delete button. After confirmation, the document is removed from the system without affecting inventory.
  • Published disassemblies cannot be deleted.

docs.title: Menu
docs.text:
The menu provides additional actions available on this page.

Available actions:

  • Print received serial number labels

For details about menu actions, see Menu actions.

docs.title: Inter warehouse
docs.text:
An Inter warehouse document is used to transfer materials from one warehouse to another. This is useful when stock needs to be moved between locations—for example, sending items from Main warehouse to Central warehouse, or transferring components to a remote storage area.

The transfer process lets you scan or search for materials, choose a destination warehouse and location, and adjust the quantities being moved. Publishing the document updates stock levels in both warehouses, ensuring each location reflects the correct quantities.

Tip

For a full demonstration, see the Inter warehouse video tutorial.

To access Inter warehouse documents, go to Logistics / Documents / Inter warehouse in the navigation.

docs.title: Schema
docs.text: Document Field Description Code System-generated unique identifier for the inter warehouse document. Document date Date when the transfer is registered. Source warehouse Warehouse from which the materials will be removed. Destination warehouse Warehouse where the materials will be received. Notes Additional remarks related to the document. Details Field Description Material The material being transferred (product, semi product, raw material, or repro material). Serial number The serial number of the unit being transferred. Best before Expiration date (for materials with shelf life). Source location Storage location in the source warehouse. Destination location Storage location where the material will be placed. Quantity (pc) Quantity to be transferred.

docs.title: List of inter warehouse documents
docs.text:
The Inter warehouse page displays all transfer documents. You can search for a specific document using the search bar, or filter the list using the left sidebar, which includes:

  • Document dates
  • View
  • Drafts — documents created but not yet published
  • Committed — published/confirmed transfers
  • Author
  • Source warehouse
  • Destination warehouse

A color indicator next to each document shows its status:

  • Green — committed
  • Gray — draft

You can click any document to open and review its details.

docs.title: Create an inter warehouse document
docs.text:
Click the action button to create a new inter warehouse document.

  1. Click Add new. Then select the Source warehouse and Destination warehouse.

  1. In the Details section, scan or type a serial number, EAN, or material name.
  2. If only one match exists → details autofill immediately.
  3. If multiple matches exist → a selection list appears:

  1. Select the correct item, and the system automatically fills all fields.
  2. Adjust Destination location or Quantity if needed.

  1. Click Save to save the detail. You can add more items by repeating step 3.
  2. Click Save on the top-left corner to save the transfer document.
  3. When the physical transfer is completed at the destination warehouse, open the draft and click Publish to confirm the stock movement.

A newly created inter warehouse document appears in Drafts. Once published, it moves to Committed and stock is transferred immediately.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: Each document includes a Notes section where you can enter any comments or additional information related to the transaction. Notes are saved together with the document and remain visible both in draft and committed versions.

docs.title: Delete an inter warehouse document
docs.text:
Draft documents can be deletedon the edit screen, but only if they contain no material entries.

If the draft still includes materials in the Details section:

  1. Click the material serial number to open the Edit detail screen.
  2. Click Delete inside the Edit detail window to remove the material.
  3. Repeat this for all remaining materials.

Once the document contains no materials, you can click Delete to remove the draft.

Committed documents cannot be deleted.

docs.title: Menu
docs.text:
The menu provides additional actions available on this page.

Available actions:

  • Print
  • Export to PDF

For details about menu actions, see Menu actions.

docs.title: Inventories
docs.text:
An Inventory document is used to verify and correct stock quantities at a specific warehouse location. It compares the theoretical stock stored in the system with the actual stock physically present on the shelves. If differences are found, you can update the quantities and publish the document to adjust the stock levels accordingly.

Inventory checks are performed per location and show all materials stored there, along with indicators of missing or excess items. You can open the Stock view by location or the Stock view by serial number directly from related screens to understand how stock levels were formed. Minimum and maximum thresholds shown in summaries can be configured in the Stock boundaries code list.

Tip

For a full demonstration, see the Inventory video tutorial.

To access Inventories, go to Logistics / Documents / Inventories in the navigation.

docs.title: Schema
docs.text: Document Field Description Code System-generated unique identifier for the inventory document. Document date Date when the inventory count is performed or recorded. Warehouse Warehouse where the inventory verification is taking place. Location Specific location within the selected warehouse that is being verified. Details Field Description Material The material stored at the selected location (product, semi product, raw material, or repro material). Location Storage location where the inventory is being performed. Theoretical (quantity) Quantity currently recorded in the system. Actual (quantity) Physically verified quantity (editable).

docs.title: List of inventory documents
docs.text:
The Inventories page displays all inventory documents. You can filter the list using the left sidebar, which includes:

  • Document dates
  • View
  • Drafts — documents created but not yet published
  • Committed — published inventory adjustments
  • Author
  • Warehouse

A color indicator next to each document shows its status:

  • Green — committed
  • Gray — draft

Click any document to open and review its contents.

List view example:

docs.title: Create an inventory document
docs.text:
Click the action button to create a new inventory document.

  1. Click Add new to create a new inventory session.

  2. Select a warehouse and location. The system automatically loads all materials recorded at that location.

  1. The Summary section displays the current inventory status:

  2. Non allocated — materials that have not yet been counted

  3. Missing — materials where the actual quantity is lower than the theoretical quantity

  4. Excess — materials where the actual quantity is higher than the theoretical quantity

  5. In the Details section, the Actual column shows 0 by default. Edit the values in this column to reflect the real number found physically at the location. When an actual value is lower or higher than the theoretical value, it will be reflected in the Missing and Excess sections of the Summary.

The Theoretical quantity is read-only. Only the Actual quantity can be edited.

  1. Once all materials have been checked and actual values are entered, the Non allocated section of the Summary will turn green and show 0.

  2. Click Publish to confirm the inventory. This action adjusts the system stock levels to match the actual physical quantities.

A newly created inventory document appears in Drafts. Once published, it moves to Committed and stock levels are corrected.

Note

The values shown under Missing and Excess indicate how many different materials have discrepancies. They do not represent the number of missing or extra pieces, only the number of materials affected.

docs.title: Edit an inventory document
docs.text: In the list view, click on a document Code to open it. In Draft status, you can modify header fields and details as needed. You can also use the menu options to print or export the document in PDF format.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: Use the Notes section to record any comments related to the inventory process.

docs.title: Delete an inventory document
docs.text:
• Click Delete in the edit screen to remove a draft inventory document. After confirmation, the document is removed from the system without affecting inventory.
  • Committed inventory documents cannot be deleted or reversed.

docs.title: Menu
docs.text:
The menu provides additional actions available on this page.

Available actions:

  • Print
  • Export to PDF

For details about menu actions, see Menu actions.

docs.title: Issues
docs.text:
An Issue document is used to record goods that come out your warehouse, for example, to be delivered to a customer. When finished products, materials, or packaged items leave the warehouse as part of a customer delivery, the Issue document captures all relevant details. Examples include issuing furniture to a customer, shipping spare parts, or delivering packaged goods as part of a sales order.

During the issuing process, you scan or search for the items being delivered, confirm the correct serial numbers or batches, and enter the quantity being dispatched. This ensures that stock levels are updated accurately and that each delivery is fully traceable.

Tip

For a full demonstration, see the Issue video tutorial.

To access Issues, go to Logistics / Documents / Issues in the navigation.

docs.title: Schema
docs.text: Document Field Description Code System-generated unique identifier for the issue document. Document date Date when the issue document is created. Warehouse Warehouse from which the materials are issued (mandatory). Customer Customer receiving the goods , selected from the Business directory (mandatory). Notes Additional remarks related to the document. Details Field Description Material Material being issued (product, semi product, raw material, or repro material). Serial number Selected serial number of the material being issued. Best before Expiration date (if the material has shelf life). Warehouse location Current storage location of the selected item. Quantity (pc) Quantity being issued.

docs.title: List of issue documents
docs.text:
The Issues page displays all issue documents. You can search for a specific document using the search bar, or filter the list using the left sidebar, which includes:

  • Document dates
  • View:
  • Drafts — documents not yet published
  • Committed — published and finalized documents
  • Author
  • Warehouse

A color indicator next to each document shows its status:

  • Green — committed
  • Gray — draft

You can click any document to open and review its details.

docs.title: Create an issue document
docs.text:
1. Click the action button to create a new document draft, then select the Warehouse and Customer.

  2. Type or scan a serial number, EAN, or material name into the Details bar.

  3. The system displays all matching materials and serial numbers.
  4. Select the correct material from the results list.

  5. The system automatically fills in all known details (material, serial number, location, best before).

    For information about working with document details, see Document details.

  6. Enter the quantity you want to issue — this is the only editable field.

  7. Click Save to add the line to the document. Add more items starting from step 2 if needed.
  8. Click Publish to commit the document.

A newly created issue document appears in the Drafts view. Once published, it moves to Committed.

docs.title: Attachments
docs.text:
Use the Attachments section to upload and manage files related to the document, such as photos, PDFs, certificates, or supporting records.

For detailed instructions, see Attachments.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: Each document includes a Notes section where you can enter any comments or additional information related to the transaction. Notes are saved together with the document and remain visible both in draft and committed versions.

docs.title: Edit an issue document
docs.text:
Click an issue document code in the main list to open its details:

  • You see the Document section (header information)
  • You see all Details representing the issued items
  • You can edit documents in Draft status
  • You can print or export draft or committed documents
  • Published (Committed) documents are read-only except for reversal creation

docs.title: Delete an issue document
docs.text:
Draft documents can be deleted on the edit screen, but only if they contain no material entries.

If the draft still includes materials in the Details section:

  1. Click the material serial number to open the Edit detail screen.
  2. Click Delete inside the Edit detail window to remove the material.
  3. Repeat this for all remaining materials.

Once the document contains no materials, you can click Delete to remove the draft.

Note

Committed documents cannot be deleted — only reversed.

docs.title: Menu
docs.text:
The menu provides additional actions available on this page.

Available actions:

  • Print
  • Export to PDF
  • Delete all details (only for draft documents)
  • Reverse issue (only for committed documents)

For details about menu actions, see Menu actions.

docs.title: Loans
docs.text:
A Loan document is used to record items that are temporarily lent out—for example, equipment lent to a customer, tools used off-site, or products provided for evaluation. When items are loaned, they become reserved and unavailable for other operations until the loan is reversed (returned).

Tip

For a full demonstration, see the Loans video tutorial.

To access Loans, go to Logistics / Documents / Loans in the navigation.

docs.title: Schema
docs.text: Document Field Description Code System-generated unique identifier for the loan document. Document date Date when the loan is created. Warehouse Warehouse from which the item is loaned (mandatory). Contact Customer or partner receiving the item, selected from the Business directory (mandatory). Notes Optional remarks related to the loan. Details Field Description Material Item being loaned (product, raw material, semi product, etc.). Serial number Selected serial number for serialized items. Best before Expiration date if applicable. Warehouse location Storage location from which the item is taken. Quantity (pc) Quantity being loaned. Must be edited before saving.

docs.title: List of loan documents
docs.text:
The Loans page displays all loan documents. You can search for a specific document using the search bar or narrow the list with the left-side filters:

  • Document dates
  • View:
  • Drafts — documents not yet published
  • Committed — published and finalized documents
  • Author
  • Warehouse

A color indicator shows status: - Green — committed - Gray — draft

Click any loan to open and review its details.

docs.title: Create a new loan
docs.text:
1. Click the action button and start a new loan draft. Select the Warehouse and Contact.
  1. In the Details section, type or scan a serial number, EAN, or material name.

The system displays: - Exact matches - All items matching your input - If multiple matches exist, a selection list appears:

  1. Choose the correct item. The system fills in known information (material, serial number, location).

  2. Enter the quantity you want to loan. Quantity must be edited in the detail form:

For information about working with document details, see Document details.

  1. Click Save to add the detail. Repeat the process to add additional loaned items.

  2. Click Publish to commit the document. When a loan is published, it moves to the Committed status and can be reviewed in the Committed list.

Once published, items in the loan become reserved and unavailable for other processes.

docs.title: Return a loan (reversal)
docs.text:
When the customer returns the loaned items, create a reversal from the document menu.

At the top-right, open the menu (hamburger icon) and select Create a new reversal.

This opens a reversal document that returns the items back to stock. For more details see Reversals.

For details about menu actions, see Menu actions.

docs.title: Edit a loan document
docs.text:
Click on the document code in the main list to open it. When you open a loan document:

  • The Document section displays header information
  • The Details list shows all loaned items
  • Draft documents can be edited
  • Committed documents are read-only except for reversal creation
  • Printing and exporting are available from the menu

docs.title: Delete a loan document
docs.text:
Draft loan documents can be deleted only if no material lines remain.

To delete:

  1. Open each detail line
  2. Click Delete inside the Edit detail screen
  3. Once all details are removed, use Delete on the document header

Note

Committed loans cannot be deleted — only reversed.

docs.title: Material analysis
docs.text:
Material analysis documents list the materials that were received and require analysis or testing based on rules configured in Material analysis management. Use this screen to review the required checks, mark materials as passed, and publish the results.

Note

Material analysis documents can be created automatically when receiving materials. Automatic creation depends on the analysis configured for the material in Material analysis management and on the system settings for the relevant material type (products, semi-products, raw materials, or repro materials). See Automatic material analysis creation.

Tip

For a full demonstration, see the Material analysis video

To access Material analysis, go to Logistics / Documents / Material analysis in the navigation.

docs.title: Schema
docs.text: Field Description Code System‑generated identifier of the material analysis document. Document date Date when the analysis document was created. Material The material under analysis (as defined by the receipt and analysis configuration). Source Serial number of the material received. Status Analysis status: Not set, Passed, or Failed.

docs.title: List of material analysis documents
docs.text: The list shows all material analysis documents created during receiving for materials with configured analyses. Use search or filters to locate entries by status.

docs.title: Review a material analysis
docs.text:
1. Click a document in the draft list to open it.
  1. Click the Material field to select the material to test (if multiple are listed).
  1. Click the Check button to pass the test for the selected material and click Save. The Status changes to Passed and the material shows green color on the list.

  • If the test is not passed, leave the check unmarked and click Save. The status changes to Failed and the material shows red color on the list. If the document is published, it appears as Failed in the Committed list.

  • Once all required checks are complete, click Publish to finalize the material analysis document. The document moves to the Committed list.

docs.title: Delete a material analysis
docs.text: Material analysis documents cannot be deleted.

docs.title: Move container
docs.text:
The Move container screen is a streamlined workflow to relocate a single container from one warehouse location to another. It is designed for fast operations (scan and confirm) without using document lists or an action button.

This flow mirrors Move serial but applies to containers (for example, pallets or boxes) that hold one or more materials.

Note

Moving a container updates inventory by moving all items inside the container from the source location to the destination location.

Tip

For a full demonstration, see the Move container video tutorial.

To access Move container, go to Logistics / Documents / Move container in the navigation.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Define warehouse Locations.
  • Ensure the container is registered and has a scannable identifier (barcode/EAN/code).

docs.title: Step 1 — Identify the container
docs.text:
Scan the container barcode or type the Container code. The UI shows container info and its current location.

  • If multiple matches are found, select the correct container.
  • If the current location is unknown, you can set it manually.

docs.title: Step 2 — Select destination
docs.text:
Choose the To location. You can: - Scan the destination location label, or - Enter the location manually.

Tip

  • Use standardized location labels to speed up scanning.
  • Verify the location’s availability if your process enforces capacity rules. See Stock boundaries for details.

docs.title: Step 3 — Confirm the move
docs.text:
Review the summary (container, from/to locations) and click Finish. The system records the transfer of the container and all contained items.

After confirmation: - The container’s location changes to the destination. - All items inside the container are shown at the destination in stock views. - All details can be reviewed in the Inter warehouse page.

docs.title: Move serial
docs.text:
The Move serial function allows you to quickly move a specific stock unit (identified by its serial number) from one storage location to another. It is designed for fast, frequent movements on the warehouse floor—for example, reorganizing shelves, preparing goods for picking, or correcting misplaced items. Unlike a full Inter warehouse document, Move serial focuses only on relocating a single serial-numbered unit within the warehouse structure.

You can open the Stock view by material or Stock view by serial number from related screens to better understand where the item is currently stored and how it has been moved in the past.

Tip

For a full demonstration, see the Move serial number video tutorial.

To access Move serial, go to Logistics / Documents / Move serial in the navigation.

docs.title: Step 1 — Scan or enter a serial number
docs.text:
Enter or scan a serial number, EAN, or type a material name.

  • If only one matching stock item exists → the system proceeds automatically.
  • If multiple matches exist → a selection screen appears.

Example (multiple matches):

Click Next to continue.

docs.title: Step 2 — Select the destination location
docs.text:
Enter the destination location by typing its name, code, or partial text.

If several locations match, you must select the correct one:

Click Next to continue.

docs.title: Step 3 — Confirm the move
docs.text:
The final screen displays:

  • The material being moved
  • Source location
  • Destination location
  • Quantity pc — total pieces stored at the source location
  • Available pc — pieces currently available for movement (editable)
  • Best before

Adjust Available pc to define how many pieces you want to move, then click Finish.

After finishing:

  • The move is immediately recorded.
  • You are returned to Step 1 so you can continue scanning additional items.
  • The completed movement is visible in Inter warehouse → Committed.

docs.title: Productions
docs.text:
A Production document records items that were produced during the execution of a Production order. Production documents are created automatically from the Execution module when a production worker records produced outputs. They increase stock for the produced items and provide traceability of what was made.

For the production‑side entry of outputs, see Execution (Outputs). Outputs are closely linked with this page: recording produced items in production creates the corresponding production document in logistics. For defining outputs on processes, see Outputs.

To access this page, go to Logistics / Documents / Productions in the navigation.

docs.title: Schema
docs.text: Document Field Description Code Unique identifier of the production document (system‑generated). Created Timestamp when the document was created. Warehouse Warehouse where the produced items were posted. Details Field Description Material Produced item (typically a product or semi product). Quantity Produced quantity recorded for the material line.

docs.title: List of production documents
docs.text:
The Productions page displays all production documents created through execution. You can filter the list using:

  • Document dates
  • View
  • Draft — production in progress (still being recorded in execution)
  • Committed — finalized production document
  • Warehouse

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
Production documents are not created manually from this page (there is no action button). They are created from the Execution module while recording outputs for a production order.

Workflow notes: - When a production worker starts recording outputs, a Draft production document is created automatically. - When the Execution process is completed, the document moves to Committed and can be reviewed in the committed list.

docs.title: Review a production document
docs.text: Click a production document code in the list to review its details. A production document contains:

docs.title: Linked documents
docs.text: If the output was recorded for a production order, the Linked documents section shows a link to the related Production order.

docs.title: Document and Details
docs.text: The Details section lists all produced items with their recorded quantities.

docs.title: Delete a production document
docs.text: Production documents cannot be deleted from the system to ensure traceability of produced items, but they can be reversed as described above.

docs.title: Menu
docs.text:
The menu provides additional actions available on this page.

Available actions:

  • Create a new reversal (only for committed documents)

For details about menu actions, see Menu actions.

docs.title: Receives
docs.text:
A Receive document is used to record the arrival of materials into your warehouse. When goods physically arrive from a supplier or another location, you create a receive document to register them in the system. Examples include receiving: - Products - Semi products - Repro materials - Raw materials

The receive process captures key information such as the material, packaging, quantity, serial numbers, best-before dates, and storage location. This ensures that stock levels are accurate and that all items are properly tracked from the moment they enter the warehouse.

Tip

For a full demonstration, see the Receive video tutorial.

To access Receives, go to Logistics / Documents / Receives in the navigation.

docs.title: Schema
docs.text:
Document Field Description Code System-generated unique identifier for the receive document. Document date Date when the goods were physically received. Warehouse Warehouse where the materials are being received (mandatory). Vendor Supplier delivering the goods, selected from the Business directory (mandatory). Supply order (Optional) Linked supply order. Notes Additional remarks related to the document. Transport and Intrastat Field Description Delivery term Delivery conditions agreed with the supplier (for example, costs and freight). Mode of transport Transport method used to deliver the goods (for example, road transport). Country dispatch Country from which the goods were dispatched. This value is typically derived from the material’s Intrastat configuration. Nature of transaction Classification of the transaction type used for Intrastat reporting (for example, direct sales or purchases). Place of delivery Indicates where the goods are delivered, according to Intrastat definitions. Details Field Description Material Material being received (product, semi product, raw material, or repro material). EAN Packaging or unit barcode. Net weight / Gross weight (kg) Weight information stored in the system or scanned. Dimensions (whd, mm) Width, height, and depth of the package. Warehouse location Storage location where the unit will be placed. Serial number Serial number scanned or generated. Best before Expiration date (for materials with shelf life). Packaging quantity (pc) Quantity represented by a single packaging unit. Quantity in base unit (pc) Quantity expressed in the material’s base measurement unit. Received quantity (pc) Quantity actually received. Number of packets Number of packages received. Details – Intrastat

This section becomes available when Intrastat reporting is enabled and the vendor is located in another EU country.

Field Description Tariff Intrastat tariff code of the material. Country origin Country where the goods were produced. Net weight (kg) Net weight used for Intrastat reporting. Invoiced amount Value of goods reported for statistical purposes. Statistical value Additional statistical amount required by national regulations.

docs.title: List of receive documents
docs.text:
The Receives page displays all receive documents. You can search for a specific document using the search bar, or filter the list using the left sidebar, which includes:

  • Document dates
  • View:
  • Drafts — documents you created but have not yet published
  • Committed — documents that are published and fixed
  • Author
  • Warehouse

A color indicator next to each document shows its status:

  • Green — committed
  • Gray — draft

You can click any document to open and review its details.

docs.title: Create a receive document
docs.text:
To create a new receive document:

  1. Click the action button, then select the Vendor.

  2. Scan or manually enter the EAN code of the packaging. The system displays all matching materials and serial numbers.

  3. The system automatically retrieves the packaging information and fills all relevant fields in the Details section.

  4. Adjust quantities, storage locations, or other values if needed.

For information about working with document details, see Document details.

  1. Click Save to save the details. Add more items starting from step 2 if needed.

  2. Click Publish to commit the document.

A newly created receive document appears in the Drafts view. Once published, it moves to Committed.

docs.title: Transport and Intrastat sections
docs.text:
When Intrastat is set to Obliged in System / Configuration / Intrastat, additional sections become available in the receive document form.

  • Transport - Used to capture logistics-related information about how the goods were delivered.
  • Intrastat - Used to collect data required for Intrastat reporting. These fields are only shown when Intrastat reporting is enabled for the system.

Note

Several Intrastat-related values are taken from material code lists (Intrastat configuration), such as country and transaction nature. These fields are not freely configurable per document and depend on predefined master data.

docs.title: Intrastat fields in Details
docs.text:
When Intrastat is enabled and the selected Vendor is from another EU country, additional fields appear inside each Detail line.

These fields are used for Intrastat statistical reporting and are required for cross-border EU transactions.

docs.title: Attachments
docs.text:
Use the Attachments section to upload and manage files related to the document, such as photos, PDFs, certificates, or supporting records.

For detailed instructions, see Attachments.

docs.title: Document connections
docs.text:
Committed receive documents include an additional Document connections section. This section lists any documents that can be created based on the received materials.

For receive documents, a Disassemble option may appear. This allows you to create a new disassembly document using the received items.

For more details, see the Disassemblies documentation.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: Each document includes a Notes section where you can enter any comments or additional information related to the transaction. Notes are saved together with the document and remain visible both in draft and committed versions.

docs.title: Edit a receive document
docs.text:
Click a document code from the list to open the edit screen. You can:

  • Review its Document section (header information)
  • Review all Details representing the received items
  • Edit draft documents
  • Print or export the document

Note

Committed documents are read-only, except for reversal creation

docs.title: Delete a receive document
docs.text:
Draft documents can be deleted on the edit screen, but only if they contain no material entries. If the draft still includes materials in the Details section, you can use the option Delete all details in the Menu.

To delete details individually:

  1. Click the material serial number to open the Edit detail screen.
  2. Click Delete inside the Edit detail window to remove the material.
  3. Repeat this for all remaining materials.

Once the document contains no materials, you can click Delete to remove the draft.

Note

Committed documents cannot be deleted — only reversed.

docs.title: Menu
docs.text:
The menu provides additional actions available on this page.

Available actions:

  • Print
  • Export to PDF
  • Delete all details (only for draft documents)
  • Reverse issue (only for committed documents)

For details about menu actions, see Menu actions.

docs.title: Reversals
docs.text:
A Reversal document is used to undo the effect of another committed document. It allows you to correct mistakes or adjust stock levels when a previously committed movement needs to be reversed. You can reverse only committed documents, and only through their Menu → Create a new reversal option. Reversals cannot be created directly from the Reversals list.

Reversals adjust stock depending on the type of document being reversed: - Reversing a Writeoff returns items to stock. - Reversing a Receive removes items again (as if they were returned to the vendor). - Reversing an Issue restores goods that were previously delivered to a customer.

Reversals can be full or partial, depending on the quantity you enter. Reversal documents themselves cannot be reversed.

Tip

For a full demonstration, see the Reversal video tutorial.

To access Reversals, go to Logistics / Documents / Reversals in the navigation.

docs.title: How reversals work
docs.text:
A reversal cancels the effect of an existing committed document without deleting or modifying the original document.

When a reversal is published:

  • The original document remains unchanged.
  • A reversal document is created and linked to the original document.
  • Opposite stock or financial effects are applied.
  • The original document is marked as partially or fully reversed.

Together, the original document and its reversal result in a net effect of zero.

Different document types produce different effects when reversed.

Examples:

  • Logistics documents reverse stock movements.
  • Financial documents reverse financial values.
  • Credit notes reverse the effect of the original credit transaction.

docs.title: Schema
docs.text: Reversed document section Field Description Document type Type of document being reversed (receive, issue, writeoff, inter warehouse). Code Identifier of the reversed document (clickable). Warehouse Warehouse where the original document was executed. Document date Date of the original document. Document Field Description Code System-generated reversal document number. Document date Date of the reversal (editable). Details Field Description Material Material being reversed (product, semi product, raw material, or repro material). Location Storage location of the reversed stock. Source quantity Quantity originally processed in the reversed document. Quantity (pc) Quantity to reverse — editable, used for partial or full reversal.

docs.title: List of reversal documents
docs.text:
The Reversals page displays all reversal documents. You can filter the list using:

  • Document dates
  • View
  • Drafts — reversal documents created but not yet published
  • Committed — confirmed reversal documents
  • Author
  • Warehouse

Each row includes:

  • The reversal document
  • The reversed document (with document type)

Color indicators:

  • Green — committed
  • Gray — draft

docs.title: Create a reversal
docs.text: Reversal documents cannot be created manually from the Reversals page. They are created only from the source document through these steps:

docs.title: Step 1 — Start the reversal
docs.text: Open the committed document you want to reverse. Open the menu and select Create a new reversal.

docs.title: Step 2 — Edit reversal quantities
docs.text:
A draft reversal document is generated automatically.

Each material line displays:

  • Source quantity
  • Editable quantity field

Examples:

  • Original writeoff: 4 pc → enter 4 for full reversal
  • Enter 2 → partial reversal

If saved but not published → it appears in Drafts

docs.title: Step 3 — Publish
docs.text:
Click Publish to confirm the reversal.

If you don’t publish immediately:

  • The reversal appears in Drafts
  • The original document shows Reversal in progress

Once published:

  • Stock levels are updated
  • The reversed document shows Partially reversed or Fully reversed
  • The reversal moves to Committed

Tags displayed on the original document:

  • Reversal in progress — when a reversal draft exists
  • Partially reversed — only part of the quantity was reversed
  • Fully reversed — the document has been completely reversed

docs.title: Edit a reversal document
docs.text:
Click a reversal document to open in the list to review its details.

Published reversals cannot be edited. Draft reversals can be edited, but keep in mind that they may affect the original document’s status (for example, if you change the quantity, the original document may switch between Reversal in progress, Partially reversed, or Fully reversed).

A reversed document contains:

docs.title: Reversed document section
docs.text: Displays information about the document being reversed and a link to open it.

docs.title: Document section
docs.text: Shows reversal code and date.

docs.title: Detail section
docs.text: Lists affected materials, their locations, original quantities, and reversed quantities.

docs.title: Delete a reversal document
docs.text:
On the edit screen, click Delete to remove a draft reversal document. After confirmation, the document is removed from the system without affecting inventory or the original document.

Committed reversals cannot be deleted.

docs.title: Simple receive
docs.text:
The Simple receive workflow provides a fast way to record incoming materials based on an existing Supply order. It guides the user through three clear steps: selecting the document header, confirming the materials to receive, and editing each detail before finishing.

Simple receive is ideal for quick warehouse operations where materials arrive exactly as ordered, without the need for advanced receiving features.

To access Simple receive, go to Logistics / Documents / Simple receive in the navigation.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Simple receive consists of three steps:

  1. Document — Select warehouse, vendor, and supply order
  2. Details — Confirm incoming materials from the supply order
  3. Edit detail — Review and complete each material line

Each completed simple receive creates a standard Receive document in the system.

docs.title: Step 1 — Document
docs.text:
In the first step, the user selects the header information for the receive document.

Fields include:

  • Warehouse — Where the materials will be received
  • Vendor — Automatically suggested if linked to the supply order
  • Supply order — Enter or scan the supply order number (for example SOR-2025-00000018)

Click Next to continue.

docs.title: Step 2 — Details
docs.text:
In this step, the system displays all expected materials and quantities from the selected supply order.

The user must now scan or manually enter the packaging code (EAN / barcode) of the item being received.

  • If the scanned code matches multiple supply order lines (for example, same material across different batches or orders), the system displays all matching items.
  • The user must select the correct line that corresponds to the received packaging.

Once the correct item is selected, the workflow automatically advances to Step 3 — Edit detail.

docs.title: Step 3 — Edit detail
docs.text:
In the final step, the user completes the information for each material line.

For each received item, you can review or adjust:

  • Warehouse location
  • Number of packets

You can also delete the line if it should not be received.

When all details are confirmed, click Finish to complete the simple receive.

docs.title: Complete the receive
docs.text:
After clicking Finish:

  • The system creates a standard completed Receive document
  • All confirmed materials are posted to stock
  • The supply order is updated with the received quantities

For more advanced receiving workflows (serial numbers, best-before dates, packaging, attachments, reversals, etc.), see the full Receives documentation.

docs.title: Menu
docs.text:
The menu provides additional actions available on this page.

Available actions:

  • Publish

For details about menu actions, see Menu actions.

docs.title: Writeoffs
docs.text:
A Writeoff document is used to record materials that must be removed from stock because they are damaged, lost, expired, or otherwise unusable. Typical examples include discarding broken items, spoiled goods, or materials damaged during handling. A writeoff lets you specify the reason, choose the affected materials, and enter the quantity to remove from stock.
