  • + Supply order – Create a Supply order directly from the inquiry

Tip

When a Supply order is created from an Inquiry, most relevant fields are automatically pre-filled.

docs.title: Complete an inquiry
docs.text:
Once the inquiry in the Available state is approved, click Complete at the top of the page. The document will now show on the Complete list.

Note

An inquiry is automatically moved to the Completed status when a new Supply order is created directly from it using the Linked documents action.

docs.title: Delete an inquiry
docs.text:
Inquiries can be deleted on the edit screen. To delete an inquiry, open the document by clicking on it in the list and then select Delete in the top-right corner.

A confirmation pop-up will appear. Click Delete again to confirm the deletion.

Note

Only draft inquiries can be deleted.

docs.title: Menu
docs.text:
The menu provides additional actions available on this page.

Available actions:

  • Print
  • Export to PDF

For details about menu actions, see Menu actions.

docs.title: Supply orders
docs.text:
A Supply order is the formal purchasing document used to confirm materials or services ordered from a vendor. It defines what your organization will receive, when, and under which conditions, and is the basis for operational workflows such as material receiving and cost center allocation.

To access this page, navigate to Supply / Documents / Supply orders in the navigation.

docs.title: How supply orders fit into the supply workflow
docs.text:
Supply orders represent the formal confirmation stage in the purchasing process.

  1. A request is usually initiated using an Inquiry.
  2. When accepted, a Supply order is created from the inquiry using the Linked documents section.
  3. Supply orders can also be created directly without an inquiry and later linked to one if needed.
  4. From a Supply order, you can create one or multiple Receive documents:
  5. Several partial receives
  6. Or a single full receive
  7. Once all materials are received, the Supply order automatically moves to the Completed status.
  8. If only partially received, it remains Available until completed.
flowchart LR
  IN[Inquiry] --> SU[Supply order] --> RE[Receive]
  classDef current fill:#cfe6f2,stroke:#0b5a80,stroke-width:3px,color:#0b1a33
  class SU current

docs.title: Schema
docs.text: Document Field Description Code System-generated identifier of the supply order. Vendor Vendor providing the materials or services, selected from the Business directory. Document date Date when the supply order is created. Supply date Planned supply or delivery date for the requested materials (mandatory). Rebate Optional discount applied to the entire supply order. Cost center Internal cost center associated with this purchase. Offer code Optional reference to the vendor’s offer or external document. Delivery – Company / Address Delivery location details, taken from the Business directory or manually adjusted if needed. Top content Predefined introductory text from Predefined texts (entity: Supply order). Bottom content Closing or legal statements from predefined texts. Details List of ordered materials or expenses, including quantities, prices, taxes, and delivery information. Details Field Description Material Material being purchased. EAN Barcode identifier for the material (optional). Quantity Ordered quantity. Supply date Specific supply date for this material line. Net price (per unit) Unit price taken from supplier material records or entered manually. Discount (%) Optional discount applied to this specific detail line. Tax rate Applied tax rule. If a 0% tax rate is defined, it is automatically applied when ordering from a supplier located outside the home country. Supplier code Vendor’s internal code/reference for the selected material. Total cost Line total (quantity × net price − discount + tax).

docs.title: Document states
docs.text:
Documents move through several possible states during their lifecycle:

  • Draft – The document is not yet published. All fields can be edited freely.
  • Committed – The document has been published. It cannot be deleted or freely modified.
    • Available – The order is valid and ready for receiving.
    • In completion – Some materials have been received (partial receiving).
    • Completed – All materials have been received and the order is fully processed.

docs.title: List view
docs.text:
The list shows all supply orders with their current status and supply dates.

At the top of the Supply orders list, the system displays two key indicators summarizing the currently filtered data.

  • Over the supply date (interactive) – Supply orders whose planned supply date has passed and are not yet fully received. Clicking this indicator automatically filters the list to show only such orders.
  • Total amount – Displays the total value (net + tax) of all supply orders included in the active filter.

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
• Document dates
  • Supply dates
  • View
  • Drafts
  • Committed
  • Available
  • In completion
  • Completed
  • Reversal state: Reversed
  • Vendor
  • Search bar

docs.title: Create a supply order
docs.text:
New supply orders can be created by clicking the action button.

See the How to create a supply order guide for a step-by-step walkthrough of the creation process.

docs.title: Edit a supply order
docs.text:
Click any supply order in the list to open it. Draft supply orders can be edited freely.

Expandable sections:

  • Linked documents
  • Attachments
  • Document
  • Delivery
  • Top content and bottom content
  • Details

docs.title: Linked documents
docs.text:
The Linked documents section allows creating and linking operational documents to a supply order.

For details about document relationships, traceability, and creating related documents, see Linked documents.

Available actions include:

  • Add project – Add project to supply order
  • + Empty receive – Create an empty receive document, ready to be updated when the actual delivery arrives
  • + Full receive – Create a full receive document (with all or part of the materials) and link it
  • Receive – Link an existing receive draft to the supply order
  • Add task – Add task to supply order
  • Copy supply order – Duplicate the supply order with its contents

docs.title: Complete a supply order
docs.text:
A Supply order is considered complete when all materials have been fully received.

Completing a supply order performs the following actions:

  • The document moves from Available to Completed state.
  • Editing becomes restricted.
  • Most Linked document actions are disabled (including creating additional Receives).
  • Any remaining open quantities are treated as fully processed.

Note

Completing a Supply order is an administrative action that finalizes its lifecycle. It does not perform additional stock movements — those occur in the linked Receive documents.

docs.title: Delete a supply order
docs.text:
Draft supply orders can be deleted on the edit screen, but only if they contain no details.

If the draft still includes items in the Details section:

  1. Click the material line to open the Edit detail screen.
  2. Click Delete inside the Edit detail window to remove the material.
  3. Repeat this for all remaining materials.

Once the document contains no materials, you can click Delete to remove the draft. If confirmed, the system removes the document permanently; otherwise, no changes are made.

Note

  • Only draft supply orders can be deleted.
  • Once a supply order is published, it can no longer be deleted.
  • Published documents cannot be deleted, but they can be reversed.

docs.title: Menu
docs.text:
This page includes menu actions in two places.

Menu actions are available through the Menu button located in the top-right corner of the list or document page.

docs.title: List menu
docs.text:
The list menu provides actions for the currently displayed list.

Available actions:

  • Export to CSV

docs.title: Document menu
docs.text:
The document menu provides actions for the currently opened document.

Available actions:

  • Print
  • Export to PDF (Supply order document) or CSV (Supply order details)
  • Send as email
  • Reverse document
  • Return to draft

For details about menu actions, see Menu actions.

docs.title: How to create a new supply order
How to create a new supply order
docs.text:
New supply orders can be created:

  • manually from the Supply orders screen using the action button
  • from an inquiry using Linked documents → + Supply order

Note

  • Supply orders created manually start with empty fields.

  • When a supply order is created from an inquiry, the system automatically pre-fills most fields from the source document, including the vendor, delivery information, and detail lines.

docs.title: Step 1 — Create the document
docs.text:
Create a new draft supply order using one of the following methods:

  • Click the action button on the Supply orders screen
  • Use Linked documents → + Supply order from a related document like an inquiry

A new draft supply order is created. If created directly from another document it will have most of its fields already pre-filled.

docs.title: Step 2 — Fill in header information
docs.text: Enter the Vendor, Document date, and Supply date (or review them if pre-filled from an inquiry document).

docs.title: Step 3 — Add details
docs.text:
Add items in the Details section. Details define the ordered items and their quantities, prices, taxes, and discounts. Each detail line corresponds to a specific material or service.

To add a new item:

  1. Type or scan a serial number, EAN, or material name in the Details bar. The system displays all matching items.

  2. Select the desired item from the list.

  3. Adjust quantity, price, discount, or tax information, then click Save.

For information about working with document details, see Document details.

docs.title: Delivery section
docs.text:
The Delivery section defines where the ordered materials will be delivered. It is filled automatically from your company's delivery information, but the address can be adjusted for each purchase if needed.

These values affect the printed supply order and the follow-up logistics documents (such as Receive documents), but they do not modify the master data stored in the Business directory.

docs.title: Attachments
docs.text:
Use the Attachments section to upload and manage files related to the document, such as photos, PDFs, certificates, or supporting records.

For detailed instructions, see Attachments.

docs.title: Top content and Bottom content
docs.text:
Pre-filled content sections allow you to add predefined text blocks to the top or bottom of the invoice. This is useful for including standard terms and conditions, payment instructions, or any other relevant information that should appear on the printed document.

The content is selected from Predefined texts.

docs.title: Linked documents
docs.text: The Linked documents section allows you to create direct connections between related documents. For example, you can link a Supply order to an Inquiry, or to one or multiple Receive documents. This helps maintain traceability and easy navigation between documents in the supply workflow.

docs.title: Step 5 — Publish the supply order
docs.text:
Once all required information has been entered, click Publish to finalize the preparation of the supply order.

After publishing, the document moves to the Committed → Available state, enabling further processes such as creating receives.

If the document is not published, it remains in the Draft state, where it can continue to be edited, updated, or published later.

docs.title: Supply stock boundaries planning
docs.text:
The Supply stock boundaries planning view helps you proactively plan purchases by identifying materials that have fallen below their defined minimum stock levels. From this screen, you can directly create Supply orders or Inquiries for the affected materials, with most details pre-filled.

This page works closely with: - Stock boundaries – where minimum and maximum quantities are defined - Supplier materials – where materials are assigned to vendors

To access this page, go to Supply / Supply stock boundaries planning.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
A material appears in this view only when all of the following conditions are met:

  1. A minimum and maximum quantity is defined in Stock boundaries
  2. The material is assigned to at least one vendor in Supplier materials
  3. The available stock is below the minimum quantity

When these conditions are fulfilled, the material becomes visible and actionable in the planning list.

docs.title: List view
docs.text:
The main list displays materials that require attention, with the following columns:

  • Material
  • Available stock
  • Minimum quantity / Maximum quantity
  • Order quantity

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
The left sidebar allows you to narrow down the results using: - Supplier - Material

Only materials matching the selected filters and planning conditions are shown.

docs.title: Row details
docs.text:
Each row can be expanded to show additional planning information, such as: - Ordered / Planned quantities - Existing Supply orders or Inquiries - Supplier - Delivery date - Price

This helps you understand whether replenishment is already in progress before creating new documents.

docs.title: Create supply orders or inquiries according to stock levels
docs.text:
Supply orders and inquiries are created directly from this screen.

  1. Select one or more materials using the checkbox and optionally adjust the Order quantity directly on the list.

  1. Click the action button and choose:
  2. Create new supply order, or
  3. Inquiry

  1. A dialog opens where you confirm:
  2. Vendor
  3. Supply date

  1. Click Create to proceed.

You are then redirected to a new Supply order or Inquiry with all relevant details—material, quantities, and vendor—already filled in.

docs.title: Supply stock boundaries planning by sales
Supply stock boundaries planning by sales
docs.text:
The Supply stock boundaries planning by sales view supports purchase planning based on sales-driven demand. It uses the same planning logic and workflow as Supply stock boundaries planning, but adds sold quantity analysis to help prioritize replenishment based on recent sales activity (regardless of status).

This view is actionable and allows you to create Supply orders and Inquiries directly, while relying on sales data to provide additional context for planning decisions.

To access this view, go to Supply / Supply stock boundaries planning by sales in the navigation.

docs.title: List view
docs.text:
The main list displays materials that require replenishment, enriched with sales-related information.

Typical columns include:

  • Material
  • Sold quantity – Quantity sold within the selected date range
  • Available stock
  • Minimum quantity / Maximum quantity
  • Ordered / Planned – Quantities already covered by existing supply documents
  • Order quantity – Suggested quantity to order

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
The left sidebar allows you to refine the planning view using:

  • Delivery date
  • Sales order
  • Material tags
  • Supplier

Only materials matching both the filters and planning conditions are displayed.

docs.title: Create supply orders or inquiries according to sales demand
docs.text:
Creating documents from this view works exactly the same way as in Supply stock boundaries planning.

  1. Select one or more materials using the checkbox and optionally type the Order quantity directly on the list.

  2. Click the action button and choose:

  3. Create new supply order, or

  4. Inquiry

  1. Choose the vendor and supply date in the dialog.

  2. Click Create to continue.

You will be redirected to a new Supply order or Inquiry with materials, quantities, and vendor information pre-filled.

For detailed action behavior, deletion rules, and document handling, refer to:

  • Supply stock boundaries planning

docs.title: Expenses
docs.text:
The Expenses code list contains all costs that your organization wants to register as predefined expenses. These can include recurring services, equipment-related costs, subcontractor fees, or any operational or financial cost that needs to be referenced in supply or production processes.

This list helps maintain consistency by storing all expenses in one place, making them available for use across documents and operational workflows.

To access this code list, go to Supply / Management / Expenses in the navigation.

docs.title: Schema
docs.text: General Field Description Code Unique identifier of the expense. Name Descriptive name of the expense. Tax rate Tax rate applied to the expense. Item price net Default net price of the expense item. Enabled Indicates whether the expense is available for use in documents. Subcontractor Business partner providing the subcontracted service, selected from the Business directory. Cost per unit (€) Cost of this subcontracted operation per unit. Operations List of operations associated with this subcontractor cost. Operation Field Description Processes Process in which the operation is used. Version Version of the selected process. Operation Specific operation belonging to the selected process and version. Ledger Field Description Account Ledger account used for postings generated from this expense. Tax entry type Tax handling classification for the expense (for example, Stock, Standard expense, Real estate). Asset type Nature of the purchase used for reporting (for example, Goods, Services). Deduct tax Indicates whether input tax is deductible for this expense. Self taxing Indicates whether reverse charge/self-taxing applies. Ignore for financial stock The expense is recorded but not included in the financial value of stock when processing invoices.

docs.title: List of expenses
docs.text:
The list displays all defined expenses along with their default net item price.

Each record includes a status indicator to the left of its name: - Blue indicates the expense is enabled - Gray indicates the expense is disabled

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
The left sidebar contains two filters:

  • Enabled
  • Disabled

These filters control whether the list shows active or inactive expense entries.

docs.title: Create a new expense
docs.text:
Click the action button to create a new expense. The input form includes sections:

  • Add new expense
  • Ledger
  • Subcontractor cost

Enter the required information and the cost of the expense in Item price net field, if known. Click Save to create the expense. The new record will then appear in the list.

Note

The cost of the expense will be automatically filled in a supply order if the expense is added as a line item and the Item price net is known.

docs.title: Subcontractor cost
docs.text:
This optional section allows adding subcontractor-related costs. You can specify:

  • Subcontractor
  • Cost per unit (€)
  • Operations

Click Add operation to open the operation selection dialog.

After entering the information, click Add to save the record or Cancel to return to the list.

docs.title: Ledger
docs.text:
In this section we assign the expense to the appropriate ledger account. See Chart of Accounts.

The options available in this section determine how the expense is handled in financial postings and reporting. They include: - Deduct tax - Self taxing - Ignore for financial stock

These can later be reset on the received invoice if needed.

docs.title: Edit an expense
docs.text:
To edit an expense, click the entry in the list and the system opens the edit mode.

All fields—including subcontractor cost and operations—can be modified. You can enable or disable an expense using the Enabled checkbox.

When you are done editing, click Save. If you do not want to save the changes, click Cancel.

docs.title: Delete an expense
docs.text:
click the entry in the list and the system opens the edit mode and click Delete to remove the expense permanently after confirmation.

Note

  • Deletion is allowed only if the expense is not referenced in dependent records.
  • Disabled expenses remain in the system but cannot be selected in new documents.

docs.title: Supplier materials
docs.text:
Supplier materials represent the list of materials that vendors provide to your organization. Each entry links an existing material from the Materials domain with a specific vendor and includes additional information such as the supplier’s material code, price, and delivery time.

This code list ensures that procurement processes can correctly identify which materials are available from each vendor and at what cost.

To access this code list, go to Supply / Management / Supplier materials in the navigation.

docs.title: Schema
docs.text: Field Description Vendor Vendor providing the material. Must exist in the Business directory (mandatory). Material type Type of material (Raw material, Semi-product, Product, Repro material). Must match an existing material type (mandatory). Material Material supplied by the vendor. Must already exist in the Materials domain (mandatory). Supplier code The vendor’s internal code for this material. Price Net price at which the vendor supplies the material. Delivery date Delivery time expressed in days.

docs.title: List of supplier materials
docs.text:
The user interface contains a list of all supplier materials, showing:

  • Vendor
  • Material (with its code and name)
  • Price

A search field is available in the upper-right corner.

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
The left sidebar contains the following filters:

  • Vendor
  • Material type
  • Entity

These filters allow narrowing the results based on supplier and material category.

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
Click the action button to display the available actions:

  • New
  • Import

docs.title: Create a new supplier material
docs.text:
Click the action button and select New. The input form includes fields:

  • Vendor
  • Material type
  • Material
  • Supplier code
  • Price
  • Delivery date

After entering the required information, click Add to save the record or Cancel to return to the list view.

docs.title: Import supplier materials
docs.text:
Click the action button and select Import. This functionality allows bulk creation or updating of supplier materials using a spreadsheet file.

This screen behaves similarly to the Import materials page. It provides:

  • File type selection (CSV or XLSX)
  • Downloadable example file
  • Drag-and-drop upload area
  • Preview of past imports

docs.title: Spreadsheet structure
docs.text:
A supplier materials import file must contain the following columns:

SupplierName,MaterialCode,Price,SupplierCode,DeliveryDate

Example row:

Rivermark Woodwork,CODE003,20,SupplierMaterial001,0

docs.title: Edit a supplier material
docs.text:
To edit an existing supplier material, click its entry in the list. The system opens the edit view where all fields can be modified.

When you are done editing, click Save. If you do not want to save the changes, click Cancel.

docs.title: Delete a supplier material
docs.text:
Click on a supplier material and click Delete to remove it from the system. A confirmation pop-up will appear. After confirming the deletion, the record will be permanently removed from the system.

Note

A supplier material can be deleted only if it is not referenced by other records.

docs.title: Menu
docs.text:
This page includes menu actions in two places.

Menu actions are available through the Menu button located in the top-right corner of the list or document page.

docs.title: List menu
docs.text:
The list menu provides actions for the currently displayed list.

Available actions:

  • Export to CSV

docs.title: Document menu
docs.text:
The document menu provides actions for the currently opened document.

Available actions:

  • Export to CSV

For details about menu actions, see Menu actions.

docs.title: Supply configuration
docs.text:
Configure Supply settings affecting document numbering. Any changes are saved automatically.

To access this page, go to Supply / Management / Configuration in the navigation.

docs.title: Document numbering settings
docs.text:
Choose the numbering model and format for Supply orders.

Field Description Document numbering model • Incremental for each year: sequence resets annually. • Incremental: a global sequence that never resets. Document code format Pattern defining structure (for example, PREFIX‑YEAR-NUMBER).

docs.title: Supply order details
docs.text:
The Supply order details view provides an aggregated list of all order items from incoming supply order documents. This view is analytical only — it does not create or change supply orders.

To access this view, go to Supply / Views / Supply order details in the navigation.

docs.title: Indicators
docs.text:
At the top of the Supply order details list, the system displays key indicators that summarize the currently filtered items. These indicators give an immediate overview of the supply order line statuses, which is especially helpful when managing large volumes of incoming materials.

Clicking any of the indicators automatically filters the list to show only the corresponding items.

The following indicators are shown:

  • All – The total number of supply order items matching the current filter criteria.
  • Closed – Items that have been fully delivered or items whose delivery date has passed and are therefore considered closed.
  • Open – Items that are still pending delivery, either fully undelivered or only partially delivered.

docs.title: Supply order details list
docs.text:
Each line in the list represents a single supply order item, including:

  • Material – The material being supplied (name, code, and link to the supply order document)
  • Delivery details – Vendor and expected delivery date
  • Quantity – Ordered quantity
  • Delivered quantity – Shows confirmed vs. unconfirmed delivery
  • Example: 50 m (Confirmed: 50 m / Unconfirmed: 0 m)

This allows you to see what has been delivered, what remains open, and what has reached or passed its delivery date.

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
The left sidebar contains filtering options to help analyze and locate supply order items:

  • Supply date – Filter by expected supply date
  • Document dates – Filter by supply order document date range
  • Detail status
  • All
  • Available
  • In completion
  • Completed
  • Document status
  • Available
  • Completed
  • Vendor – Filter supply items by supplier

These filters allow you to narrow results to only the materials, delivery dates, and statuses relevant to your planning.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This view is designed for:

  • Monitoring upcoming supply deliveries
  • Checking which supply order items are fully or partially delivered
  • Reviewing unconfirmed vs. confirmed delivered quantities
  • Tracking vendor-specific incoming materials
  • Supporting supply planning and warehouse preparation

It complements the Supply orders document screen by focusing on items, not documents.

docs.title: Supply orders report
docs.text:
The Supply orders report view provides a consolidated overview of ordered materials and services, grouped by supplier. It is designed for analysis and reporting purposes and does not create or modify documents.

To access this page, go to Supply / Views / Supply orders report.

docs.title: Purpose of this view
docs.text:
Supply orders reports help you:

  • Analyze ordered quantities and values per supplier
  • Review order history for specific materials
  • Understand average prices and total ordered costs
  • Quickly drill down into procurement performance without opening individual documents

This view is read-only and reflects data from committed Supply orders.

docs.title: Layout and structure
docs.text:
The report is organized hierarchically:

  • Suppliers act as top-level groups
  • Under each supplier, ordered materials are listed
  • Each material row aggregates data from all relevant Supply orders

For each material, the report shows: - Ordered quantity - Average price - Total cost, including net value and tax

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
The filters on the left allow you to narrow down the report:

  • Supply date — Filter orders within a specific date range.
  • Vendor — Show order data for one or more selected suppliers.
  • Product — Show order data for materials destined for specific products (for example, Pine wood board for Pine wood table).

Filters can be combined to focus on very specific procurement scenarios.

docs.title: Interpretation of values
docs.text:
• Quantity represents the total ordered quantity for the material
  • Average price is calculated across all matching Supply orders
  • Total cost shows:
  • Net price
  • Tax amount
  • Final total value

All amounts are calculated based on the Supply orders included by the selected filters.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Only committed supply orders are included in this report.
  • Draft or reversed supply orders are not shown.
  • The view is intended for analysis only and does not support actions such as editing, reversing, or creating documents.

For detailed document-level information, open the related Supply orders directly from the Supply / Documents / Supply orders section.

docs.title: System
docs.text:
The System domain contains administrative tools used to configure, secure, and maintain the platform.

Unlike operational domains such as Sales, Supply, or Production, the System domain is primarily intended for administrators and advanced users responsible for system setup, user management, integrations, and global configuration.

To access this domain, navigate to System from the sitemap.

Note

Available options depend on the enabled modules, installed extensions, and user permissions.

docs.title: What is included in the System domain?
docs.text:
The System domain is organized into several administrative areas:

  • Configuration – global system and organizational settings
  • Users – user accounts and access management
  • Security – authentication and access control
  • Subscriptions – licensing and subscription management
  • Client registration – registration and identification settings
  • Development – technical and developer-focused tools
  • Workers – background processing and system services

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The Configuration area contains settings that affect the behavior of the entire platform.

Examples include:

  • Organizational information
  • Default country and currency
  • Warehouse settings
  • Fiscalization settings
  • Connectivity and integration settings
  • Localization options

Available configuration entries may vary depending on installed modules and country-specific requirements.

See:

  • Configuration
  • Warehouse configuration
  • Sales Retail SI Settings

docs.title: Users
docs.text:
The Users section manages access to the platform.

Administrators can:

  • Create user accounts
  • Assign roles and permissions
  • Manage user status
  • Configure localization settings

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
The Security section contains authentication and authorization settings used to protect access to the platform and its data.

Available options depend on the deployment model and enabled security features.

docs.title: Subscriptions
docs.text: The Subscriptions section contains licensing and subscription-related information used to manage access to platform features and services.

docs.title: Client registration
docs.text:
Client registration contains settings and information related to system registration and identification.

Available options may vary depending on deployment and licensing requirements.

docs.title: Development
docs.text:
The Development section contains technical tools intended for developers, consultants, and advanced administrators.

These tools are typically used during implementation, customization, troubleshooting, and integration activities.

docs.title: Workers
docs.text:
The Workers section provides information about background services and automated processes executed by the platform.

Depending on configuration, these services may be responsible for:

  • Scheduled tasks
  • Notifications
  • Synchronization jobs
  • Integration processing
  • Other automated operations

docs.title: System and Other Domains
docs.text:
The System domain supports all other domains throughout the platform.

Area Interaction Sales Supplies fiscalization, organization, and user settings. Supply Provides warehouse and integration settings. Production Supplies user, localization, and system-wide configuration. Maintenance Provides access control and shared configuration. Resources Uses users, roles, and localization settings.

The System domain acts as the administrative foundation of the platform and supports the operation of all business processes.

docs.title: Users
docs.text:
The Users code list contains all user accounts registered in the system. User accounts define login credentials, role-based access rights, personal profile details (name, email, time zone, language), and whether the user may access specific system areas (warehouse/domain rules still under review). These settings ensure that each user has appropriate permissions according to their responsibilities.

To access the Users page, go to System / Users in the navigation.

docs.title: Schema
docs.text: Field Description First name User’s given name. Last name User’s family name. Email Email address used for account identification and communication. Username Login name used for signing into the system. Roles One or more system roles determining access rights. PIN Optional numeric code for simplified authentication scenarios. Security code Optional additional authentication code (usage rules may vary by system). Status User status: Active, Inactive, or Locked. Time zone Defines the user’s default time zone for all date- and time-related operations. Language User interface language (Default, Slovenian, English).

docs.title: Management
docs.text:
You can access the Users code list from System / Users in the navigation. The list displays all system users with their status indicators:

  • Green — Active
  • Grey — Inactive or Locked

You may search, sort, or open a user to edit its details.

docs.title: Create a new user
docs.text:
Click the action button to create a new user.

The form includes personal details, login credentials, assigned roles, and localization settings.

Available Membership roles can be selected from the dropdown:

Click Add to create the user or Cancel to return to the list.

Note: Roles define the user’s access rights within the system. Role structures are configured individually, according to your business model and operational needs. Because of this, the exact meaning and scope of each role may differ between implementations.

docs.title: Edit a user
docs.text:
To modify an existing user, click the user’s Name in the list. The edit screen allows updating all fields, including roles and status.

Click Save to confirm changes or Cancel to discard them.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The Configuration section, found under System / Configuration, contains global system settings that define core organizational and localization behavior.

Important

These settings are referenced by nearly all modules (Sales, Supply, Logistics, Projects, etc.) and must be configured before operational work begins.

While the System / Configuration area contains numerous technical settings that affect the system's overall behavior, this document focuses on two key groups that must be configured for initial setup:

  • Common Types → Common Types Settings
  • System → Organization

These two configuration groups must be set up during the initial system setup, as they influence all modules across the platform.

Warning

These settings affect every domain. Only system administrators should modify them.

docs.title: Common Types Settings
docs.text:
The Common Types Settings section defines the default country and default currency used throughout the platform. Many modules rely on these values for correct formatting, taxation, legal structure, and document output.

To access these settings go to CommonTypes / CommonTypes Settings in the left sidebar and click on Organization.

docs.title: Country
docs.text:
Select the country where the organization operates. This setting controls localization and regulatory defaults across documents and modules.

Important

The selected country must already exist in the Countries code list. If not configured there first, it will not appear in the dropdown menu.

docs.title: Currency
docs.text:
Select the default currency for the organization. This setting controls monetary formatting and default document currency across modules and reports.

Important

The selected currency must already exist in the Currencies code list.

These two settings form the foundation for all financial and commercial operations across the platform.

docs.title: Organization
docs.text:
The Organization section defines your company’s identity and legally required business information. These values appear on printed documents such as invoices, delivery notes, sales orders, and supply orders.

To access these settings, go to System / Organization.

docs.title: Schema
docs.text: Field Description Logotype Upload the company logotype used on official documents. Accepted formats: PNG, JPG. Upload via drag-and-drop or file dialog. Name Full legal name of the company. Address Street name and number, including city or municipality. Post Postal code of the registered business address. Website Displayed on various sales and supply documents. Email Primary contact email for customer or supplier communication. Phone number General contact number displayed on documents. Registration number Official company registration number. Tax number Tax identification number (for example, VAT ID). Document footer text Formatted footer appearing on documents across the system. Typical contents: company name, full address, website, email, phone number, legal statements or disclaimers. Supports multiline formatting. Signature of the responsible person Upload the signature image used on selected official documents. Accepted formats: PNG, JPG. Displayed on invoices, confirmations, and similar outputs.

docs.title: Production order configuration
docs.text:
Production order configuration settings define the default behavior of production orders, including their initial status, completion rules, and material consumption behavior.

To access these settings, go to System / Configuration in the navigation, then select Production orders / Settings in the left sidebar.

docs.title: Allow adding inputs to consumption
docs.text:
When enabled, additional input materials can be added directly to a consumption entry.

When disabled, consumption is limited to the input materials already defined for the production operation.

docs.title: Production order
docs.text: The Production order section defines how production orders behave when they are created and completed.

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
Defines the default status assigned to a production order when it is created.

New production orders have a Draft status by default when first create. Select a different status when you require new production orders to have a different status, for example Active

docs.title: Parent threshold
docs.text:
Defines the percentage tolerance allowed when determining whether a parent production order can be completed based on the actual quantities produced by its child production orders.

For example, if the parent production order has a planned quantity of 100 and the Parent threshold is set to 5, a combined actual quantity of 95 from the child production orders is considered sufficient to fulfill the parent order.

A value of 0 means that no quantity deviation is allowed.

Note

This setting applies to production orders that contain child production orders.

docs.title: Auto close production order
docs.text:
When enabled, the production order is automatically closed after all of its operations are completed.

When disabled, the production order must be closed manually after the operations are completed.

docs.title: Sales Retail SI Settings
docs.text:
The Sales Retail SI Settings are used to configure the connection with the FURS (Financial Administration of the Republic of Slovenia) for fiscalization of retail invoices.

These settings enable the system to send tax-relevant data for retail issued invoices to FURS.

To access these settings, navigate to System / Configuration/ Sales.Retail.SI / Sales Retail SI Settings.

Note

The SI suffix indicates that these settings apply to Slovenia. If another country is selected (for example Croatia), the available settings may differ according to local fiscalization requirements.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Fiscalization requires a secure connection to FURS using digital certificates. These certificates are issued by FURS and are required to authenticate the company when submitting invoice data.

More information about certificates and technical specifications is available on the official FURS portal.

docs.title: Certificates
docs.text:
The configuration includes two types of certificates:

  • Test – sends data to the FURS test system
  • Production – sends data to the live FURS system

Switching this option changes where fiscal data is submitted.

docs.title: Schema
docs.text: Field Description Active certificate Defines which environment is used for connection to FURS: • Test – sends data to the test system • Production – sends data to the live system FURS private test certificate Digital certificate used for connection to the FURS test environment Test certificate password Password for accessing the test certificate Test certificate company tax number Company tax number used in the test environment FURS private production certificate Digital certificate used for connection to the FURS production environment Production certificate password Password for accessing the production certificate Automatic FURS confirmation If enabled, invoices are automatically sent to FURS when issued

docs.title: Warehouse configuration
docs.text: Warehouse configuration settings allow you to customize how the system handles various warehouse operations, such as inventory management and GS1 settings. These settings can be accessed and modified by navigating to Warehouse in the sidebar menu.

docs.title: GS1 settings
docs.text: The GS1 parser configuration defines how the system interprets GS1 barcodes when scanning items during processes such as receiving or production.

docs.title: GS1 parser separator character
docs.text:
Specifies the separator character used to split GS1 data elements (Application Identifiers) within a scanned barcode. This character is used to detect the end of variable-length fields (such as batch/lot number).

Important

The value must be entered in Unicode (hexadecimal) format (for example 0x001D).

To enter GS1 identification details go to Warehouse / Settings / GS1 settings in the sidebar menu (see below).

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Warehouse settings allow you to configure key application parameters, including database connectivity, GS1 identification, inventory behavior, and warehouse rules.

docs.title: Email list
docs.text: Use this section to define email-related configurations (for example recipients for notifications or system messages).

docs.title: GS1 Settings
docs.text:
Configures GS1 identification used for barcode generation and parsing.

  • GS1 Identity – The company’s GS1 prefix assigned by a GS1 authority. This value is used when generating GS1-compliant codes such as:
    • GTIN (product codes)
    • SSCC (logistics units)

docs.title: Inventory
docs.text: • Show theoretical column – When enabled, displays the theoretical quantity column while the document is in draft status.

docs.title: Warehouse location settings
docs.text: • Disallow warehouse location from a different warehouse on inter move documents – Prevents selecting locations that belong to a different warehouse when creating inter-warehouse movement documents.

docs.title: Automatic material analysis creation
docs.text:
The Auto create settings control whether the system automatically creates a material analysis when materials are inserted.

To access these settings, go to System / Configuration, then select WarehouseExtSettings / Settings in the left sidebar.

Available options:

  • Auto create product analysis – automatically creates a material analysis when a product is inserted.
  • Auto create semi product analysis – automatically creates a material analysis when a semi-product is inserted.
  • Auto create raw material analysis – automatically creates a material analysis when a raw material is inserted.
  • Auto create repro material analysis – automatically creates a material analysis when a repro material is inserted.

Enable only the material types for which analyses should be created automatically.

docs.title: Create and maintain a knowledge base
Create and maintain a knowledge base
docs.text:
This tutorial explains how to create a structured Knowledge base that users can browse, search, and maintain over time.

You will create:

  • Directory tags for categorization
  • Directories to organize content
  • Articles containing documentation
  • A table of contents for navigation

At the end of the tutorial, users will be able to browse and search documentation through the Knowledge base.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Create a knowledge base that:

  • Organizes documentation into logical topics
  • Provides clear navigation through a table of contents
  • Supports searching and filtering by tags
  • Allows content to be maintained over time

docs.title: 1. Plan the knowledge structure
docs.text:
Before creating content, identify the topics you want to document.

Typical examples include:

  • Work instructions
  • Safety procedures
  • Quality guidelines
  • Maintenance procedures
  • Frequently asked questions
  • Employee onboarding materials

Think about:

  • Which directories will be needed
  • Which articles belong to each directory
  • How users should navigate the content

Tip

Start with a simple structure and expand it over time.

docs.title: 2. Create directory tags
docs.text:
Directory tags help users find content through search and filtering.

Examples:

  • Assembly
  • Quality
  • Safety
  • Packaging
  • Maintenance

  1. Open Knowledge / Management / Directory tags.
  2. Create the tags required for your documentation.
  3. Save the tags.

docs.title: 3. Create directories
docs.text:
Directories are the main containers used to organize knowledge content.

Examples:

  • Work Instructions
  • Quality Management
  • Safety Procedures
  • Maintenance

  1. Open Knowledge / Management / Directories.
  2. Create a new directory.
  3. Enter a name, key, and optional description.
  4. Save the directory.

docs.title: 4. Create articles
docs.text:
Articles contain the actual documentation users will read.

Examples:

  • Assemble table frame
  • Packaging procedure
  • Daily equipment inspection

  1. Open Knowledge / Management / Directories.
  2. Select Articles from the desired directory.
  3. Click the action button to create a new article.
  4. Enter:
  5. Title
  6. Key
  7. Content
  8. Optionally: * Add attachments. * Enable comments. * Schedule publication or expiration dates.
  9. Assign relevant tags.
  10. Save the article.

For details, see Articles.

docs.title: 5. Build the table of contents
docs.text:
The table of contents defines how users navigate the directory.

  1. Open Knowledge / Management / Directories.
  2. Select Table of contents for the desired directory.
  3. Create folders to organize articles into topics.
  4. Add articles to the folders.
  5. Arrange entries using ordinal values to define the order.

For details, see Table of contents.

Example:

Work Instructions
├── Assembly
│   ├── Assemble table frame
│   └── Install tabletop
├── Packaging
│   └── Packaging procedure
└── Maintenance
    └── Daily equipment inspection

Note

The table of contents controls navigation only. Article content is managed separately.

docs.title: 6. Review the Knowledge base
docs.text:
Once directories, articles, and navigation have been configured:

  1. Open Knowledge / Knowledge base.
  2. Locate your directory.
  3. Open the directory.
  4. Browse articles using the table of contents.
  5. Verify search and tag filtering.

Users can:

  • Filter by tags
  • Browse directories
  • Open articles
  • Download attachments
  • Add comments (if enabled)

For details, see Knowledge base.

docs.title: 7. Maintain content
docs.text:
A knowledge base should be reviewed regularly.

Recommended practices:

  • Keep articles concise and focused
  • Use consistent naming conventions
  • Remove duplicate content
  • Review outdated information periodically
  • Use tags consistently
  • Disable unused directories when necessary
  • Use publication and expiration dates when appropriate

Tip

Assign responsibility for maintaining each directory to a specific person or team.

docs.title: Example: Creating a work instruction library
docs.text:
A manufacturing company wants to centralize shop-floor documentation.

  1. Create tags:

  2. Assembly

  3. Packaging

  4. Maintenance

  5. Create a directory:

  6. Work Instructions

  7. Create articles:

  8. Assemble table frame

  9. Packaging procedure

  10. Daily equipment inspection

  11. Build the table of contents:

  12. Assembly

  13. Packaging

  14. Maintenance

  15. Review the directory in the Knowledge base.

Operators can now search instructions, browse documentation by topic, and access the latest approved procedures from a single location.

docs.title: Improving production efficiency
docs.text:
This guide explains, in simple steps, how to track production work and improve results. You will record what was done (materials used, outputs, loss, downtime, effort) and then use clear reports and KPIs to find bottlenecks and decide what to fix first.

flowchart LR
  A[Define processes tags] --> B[Execute record] --> C[Review KPIs and Summaries] --> D[Act on findings]

Goal: record actual work (consumed, loss, downtime, effort) and review KPIs and summaries to find bottlenecks.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Processes and resources: Processes, Inputs, Outputs
  • Classification tags: Loss classification tags, Downtime tags
  • People and roles: Job positions, Human resources
  • (Optional) Warehouse locations for materials: Warehouse locations

docs.title: 1. Define processes and standards
docs.text:
• Open Processes and define operations, inputs, outputs, and expected cycle times.
  • Ensure Inputs and Outputs exist for all materials and products.

Note

Clear process definitions enable accurate consumption and performance calculations during execution.

docs.title: 2. Prepare tags and resources
docs.text:
• Add Loss classification tags for scrap, rework, quality issues.
  • Add Downtime tags for equipment stops and delays.
  • Verify Human resources and Non-human resources as needed.

Tip

Keep the tag list short and meaningful so operators can select correct reasons quickly.

docs.title: 3. Record execution
docs.text:
• Use Execution to record:
  • Consumed materials
  • Produced outputs
  • Loss (scrap/rework) with reasons
  • Downtime with reasons
  • Effort (labor time)

Tip

Use Linked documents in Production orders to trace consumption per order, then compare recorded use with Stock and movement documents (Inter warehouse, Move serial) to confirm differences and identify causes.

docs.title: 4. Review KPIs and summaries
docs.text:
• Open analytics to evaluate performance:
  • Production KPIs — overview of throughput, efficiency, and quality
  • Loss Summary — scrap and rework by reason and period
  • Downtime Summary — equipment stops by reason and duration
  • Equipment Summary — performance per machine/line
  • Organization Unit Loss — loss by organizational unit
  • Organization Unit Downtime — downtime by organizational unit

Tip

  • Filter by time range and unit, then compare top reasons to prioritize improvements.

  • For cost insights:

  • In the list of closed Production orders, review unit cost with arrows indicating change vs. previous order.
  • Open Work items costs to compare unit cost trends per order and see the cost breakdown of Materials, Effort, and Expenses with charts (Cost, Distribution, Performance).

docs.title: 5. Act on findings
docs.text:
• Update process standards or training if frequent loss reasons appear.
  • Schedule maintenance or adjust planning for recurring downtime.
  • Adjust material flow or stock locations if consumption variances are high.

Tip

  • Keep data entry simple (preset tags, defaults) to improve operator adoption.
  • Review KPIs regularly (that is, weekly); act on one improvement at a time.
  • Revisit tags quarterly to merge duplicates and keep reasons actionable.

docs.title: Example: Improving efficiency in a packaging line
docs.text:
A mid-size packaging branch noticed high scrap and frequent short stops.

  1. Define processes and tags
  2. Set expected time per unit/batch in Operations, defined on Human resources and Non‑human resources; ensured all Inputs/Outputs were set.
  3. Created concise tags: Loss = "Label misprint", "Seal defect"; Downtime = "Printer jam", "Film change".
  4. Record execution for one week
  5. Operators logged consumed film and labels, outputs, and selected loss/downtime reasons per batch in Execution.
  6. Review KPIs and summaries
  7. Loss Summary showed 3.2% scrap driven by "Label misprint" on the afternoon shift.
  8. Downtime Summary highlighted frequent "Printer jam" totaling 2.4 hours/week.
  9. Checked unit cost trends in Work items costs and the closed list in Production orders to confirm material cost impact.
  10. Act on findings
  11. Trained operators on label alignment; replaced worn printer rollers.
  12. Adjusted replenishment to pre-stage film rolls to reduce changeover time.
  13. Validate results
  14. Next month: scrap dropped to 1.1%; downtime from jams fell by 60%. Throughput improved by 8%.

docs.title: Execution – Quick User Guide
docs.text:
This guide shows the essential steps to perform production using the Execution screen.

Note

For more information and details refer to the full Execution documentation.

docs.title: 1. Select your production order
docs.text:
When you open Execution: - Make sure the correct organizational unit is selected. - Select the production order and operation you will work on.

If nothing is selected, or no production orders are available, the screen will prompt you to choose a Production order.

docs.title: 2. Start the operation
docs.text: You can start work in two ways:

docs.title: Option A — Press Start
docs.text: Tap Start to begin timing and working on the operation.

docs.title: Option B — Press Produce
docs.text: Pressing Produce will automatically start the operation, even if you don’t change the quantity.

docs.title: 3. Produce items
docs.text:
1. Enter the number of items you produced (for example, 1).
  2. Press Produce.
  3. The system updates:
  4. Produced quantity
  5. Remaining quantity

Repeat whenever more items are completed.

NOTE Review Instructions if they appear or whenever needed: - Tap Instructions to view assembly steps, visuals, or operation-specific notes.

docs.title: 4. Complete quality checklists (if applicable)
docs.text:
Checklists and quality controls are simple step-by-step checks that help keep work safe and products correct. A checklist can pop up at the start, during the job, or before you finish, based on how the operation is set up.

  1. Follow the steps shown on screen.

  1. Complete each step. When you’re done, tap Finish.
  2. If you need to do a checklist again:
    1. Open the action menu via the action button.
    2. Enter the Quality section.
    3. Tap Repeat for the checklist you want to redo.

Note

You can’t stop the operation if a required checklist isn’t finished.

docs.title: 5. Record losses (if applicable)
docs.text:
1. Go to the action menu by clicking the action button.
  2. Enter the Loss section.
  3. Enter the defective quantity.
  4. Select the loss reason.
  5. Confirm by clicking the yellow Loss button.

docs.title: 6. Record consumed materials
docs.text:
Use this when materials are used during the operation:

  1. Go to the action menu by clicking the action button.
  2. Enter the Consumed section.
  3. Scan, type, or select the material.
  4. Enter the quantity consumed.
  5. Confirm.

docs.title: 7. Record downtime (if applicable)
docs.text:
1. Go to the action menu by clicking the action button.
  2. Enter the Downtime section.
  3. Click start and stop to record the interruption period.
  4. Choose the reason for the interruption.
  5. Adjust the times if necessary.
  6. Save.

Use this for any interruption, such as waiting for materials or machine issues.

docs.title: 8. Record effort (working time)
docs.text:
1. Go to the action menu by clicking the action button.
  2. Enter the Effort section if required by your workflow.

docs.title: Automatic:
docs.text: Tap Start → work → tap Stop.

docs.title: Manual:
docs.text:
Open Effort, then enter: - Date - Start/end time or duration - Notes (optional)

Save the entry. The list of recorded efforts can be found below.

docs.title: 9. Finish the operation
docs.text:
When all production work is completed:

  1. Verify produced quantity.
  2. Record any losses, downtime, consumed materials, or checklists.
  3. Tap Stop to finish the operation.
