docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
Tom PIT.Connected is a global digital transformation platform. Use this guide to quickly orient yourself and navigate the materials.

This documentation is structured by platform domains (each with their documents, code lists, views, and analytics) and complemented by typical end‑to‑end workflows in the Getting started folder to help you follow common scenarios from setup to execution.

Tip

Start with the Navigation topic to explore domains, documents, and views.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
The platform follows a consistent structure:

  • Domain — business areas (for example, Production, Logistics, Sales, Supply, Assets, Projects). Each domain divided into different sections:
  • Documents — operational documents and workflows (for example, Issues, Receives, Sales orders)
  • Views and Analytics — Performance views, KPIs, and reports
  • Management — code lists and master data (for example, Business directory, Measure units, Tax rates, Payment methods, Organization bank accounts)
  • Common — shared concepts and UI elements

More information on the structure and navigation inside the platform can be found in the navigation guide.

docs.title: Scenarios
docs.text:
The following scenarios demonstrate typical end-to-end business processes and are recommended for new users becoming familiar with the platform.

  1. Prerequisites
  2. Sales process with prepayment
  3. Sales process without prepayment
  4. Improving production efficiency
  5. Restock or produce
  6. Create and maintain a knowledge base
  7. Add two-factor authentication (2FA)

docs.title: Quick user guides
docs.text:
Find quick guides for common tasks in the following documents:

  • Execution – Quick User Guide
  • Maintenance Execution – Quick User Guide

Tip

Looking for step-by-step instructions? Many document pages include a dedicated How to create... guide that walks you through the complete process of creating and publishing documents, such as How to create a sales order, How to create a production order, or How to create an issued invoice.

docs.title: Maintenance Execution – Quick User Guide
docs.text:
This guide shows the essential steps to carry out maintenance work using the Maintenance execution screen.

Note

For more information and details refer to the full Maintenance execution documentation.

docs.title: 1. Select your maintenance order
docs.text:
When you open Maintenance execution: - Make sure the correct organization unit is selected at the top of the screen. - Check that the maintenance order and operation shown are the ones you will work on.

To choose a different maintenance order, click the maintenance order in the top-left corner. In the dialog, select the order (it shows Priority, Code and Equipment) and click Select. See Select a maintenance order.

If no maintenance order is selected, or none are available, the screen will prompt you to choose one.

docs.title: 2. Start the operation
docs.text:
Press Start to begin the current operation. The operation becomes active and the execution time starts to be recorded. See Start maintenance.

If you need to interrupt the work, press Pause. The operation stays open and you can resume it by pressing Start again. See Pause maintenance.

docs.title: 3. Complete quality checklists (if applicable)
docs.text:
Quality checklists are simple step-by-step checks that help keep the work safe and the result correct. A checklist can pop up when the operation starts, while it is paused, or when it is stopped, depending on how the operation is set up.

  1. Follow the steps shown on screen.
  2. Complete each step. When you are done, tap Finish.
  3. To review checklists at any time, open the action button and select Quality.

Note

You can’t stop the operation if a required checklist isn’t finished.

docs.title: 4. Follow instructions (if available)
docs.text:
If instructions are defined for the operation, open the action button and select Instructions. See Instructions.

Review them before you start the task and use them as guidance while you work. They may include safety notes, step-by-step actions or visual references.

docs.title: 5. Record consumed materials (if applicable)
docs.text:
Use this when materials are used during the maintenance:

  1. Open the action button and select Inputs. See Inputs.
  2. Select the material.
  3. Enter the quantity used.
  4. Click Save.

The screen shows the consumed quantity against the planned quantity, for example 0 / 3 pc.

docs.title: 6. Record the work performed
docs.text:
1. Open the action button and select Record.
  2. Enter a description of the maintenance work performed in the free-text field.
  3. Click Save.

The saved record is also shown on the maintenance order.

docs.title: 7. Record effort (working time)
docs.text: 1. Open the action button and select Effort if required by your workflow.

docs.title: Automatic:
docs.text: Press Start → carry out the work → press Stop.

docs.title: Manual:
docs.text:
Open Effort, then enter: - Date - Start and end time or duration - Notes (optional)

Save the entry. The recorded efforts are listed below.

docs.title: 8. Finish the operation
docs.text:
When all maintenance work is completed:

  1. Check that the checklists are completed, and that materials and effort are recorded.
  2. Press Stop to finish the operation. See Complete maintenance.

The operation is marked as Completed and its completion time is recorded.

If the process has more operations, the next operation opens automatically when you stop the current one. Continue with the next operation from step 2.

When the last operation of the maintenance order is stopped, the order closes automatically.

You can also complete the maintenance order from the order itself, without stopping the remaining operations. Open the menu in the upper-right corner of the maintenance order and, under Action, select Complete maintenance order.

docs.title: 9. Reactivate a completed operation (if needed)
docs.text: A completed operation cannot be reactivated from the Maintenance execution screen. To reopen it, open the maintenance order and select Reactivate for that operation. See the note in Complete maintenance.

docs.title: Related guides
docs.text: • Execution – Quick User Guide

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Complete these steps to prepare the system for first use. This guide links to the right pages and avoids repeating details.

The system may initially be empty of the basic data required for day‑to‑day business (countries, currencies, tax rates, measure units, partners, items, warehouses, etc.). These values must be entered via the corresponding code lists before documents and workflows can be used.

Tip

Follow this guide step‑by‑step to configure the platform. Use the links to open each code list or setting if you need further details, then return to this Prerequisites page to continue with the next step.

docs.title: Overview of required steps:
docs.text:
1. Create essential common code lists: Countries, Currencies, Tax rates, Measure units, Banks
  2. Configure system settings: System configuration (organization identity, default country and currency)
  3. Configure payment settings: Payment methods, Organization bank accounts
  4. Add business partners: Business directory
  5. Add materials and assets: material types — Products, Semi products, Raw materials, Repro materials; packaging — Packaging; assets — Assets
  6. Set up warehouses and locations (if applicable): Warehouses, Locations, Organization units, Warehouse locations

Tip

A code list is shared master data used across documents and domains (for example, countries, currencies, tax rates, measure units). Configure these first so forms, dropdowns, and calculations work correctly.

docs.title: 1. Create essential Common code lists
docs.text:
These shared code lists are required by Sales, Supply, Logistics, Production, and System:

  • Countries — list of countries used for addresses, localization, and document formatting Go to: Sales / Management / Countries
  • Currencies — currencies available for pricing, documents, and financial reports Go to: Sales / Management / Currencies
  • Tax rates — VAT and other tax definitions applied on sales and supply documents Go to: Sales / Management / Tax rates
  • Measure units — base units (kilograms, meters, pieces, etc.) used for quantities and calculations Go to: Sales / Management / Measure units
  • Banks — list of banks used to register organization and partner bank accounts Go to: Sales / Management / Banks

Note

Domains and System settings depend on these values for correct behavior.

Important

Common code lists must be created before selecting them in System configuration or domain documents. See Common domain for details.

docs.title: 2. Configure System settings
docs.text: Set the organization and global defaults used across all modules: - System configuration — organization identity, legal data, footer; default country and currency Go to: System / Configuration - Configure Organization (identity, legal details, footer) - Set Common Types (default Country, default Currency)

docs.title: 3. Configure payment settings (Sales)
docs.text:
If your scenarios include Sales documents, configure payment data: - Payment methods — supported customer payment types (bank transfer, card, cash, etc.) Go to: Sales / Management / Payment methods - Organization bank accounts — company bank accounts shown on invoices and used for payments Go to: Sales / Management / Organization bank accounts

Note

Invoices and prepayments require valid payment definitions.

docs.title: 4. Add business partners (Business directory)
docs.text:
Add business partners (customers, vendors, cooperators) to use them across procurement, sales, and logistics: - Business directory — centralized list of customers, suppliers, and partner entities Go to: Sales / Management / Business directory

Note

Documents need partner data (customer, supplier) to be created.

docs.title: 5. Materials and Assets
docs.text:
Add materials and assets that will be used in documents and stock operations according to your use-case: - Material types: - Products — finished goods you sell or stock - Semi products — intermediate goods used in production - Raw materials — base materials consumed in production - Repro materials — consumables and auxiliary materials (screws, glue, varnish)

Go to: Assets / Materials - Packaging: - Packaging — defines how a material is packaged (quantity, weight, dimensions, optional alternative measure units) - Assets: - Assets — catalog of goods and services with pricing and tax info. Go to: Assets / Assets

Note

Sales and production documents require defined items and resources.

docs.title: 6. Set up warehouses and locations (if applicable)
docs.text:
For logistics or production scenarios involving stock: - Warehouses — storage sites where stock is held Go to: Logistics / Management / Warehouses - Locations — bin/shelf locations inside warehouses for precise placement Go to: Logistics / Management / Locations - Organization units — production areas, lines, or cells used for planning and execution Go to: Production / Management / Organization units - Warehouse locations — links organization units to physical warehouse locations for staging inputs/outputs Go to: Production / Management / Warehouse locations

Note

Stock operations require defined storage sites and locations.

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text: You have now added the minimum required data to carry out a standard business process. With core code lists, system defaults, payment setup, partners, items, and storage locations in place: - Forms and dropdown menus resolve correctly across domains - Documents can be created without missing mandatory values - Stock movements and invoices can be executed end-to-end

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text: Explore end-to-end scenarios to see how these prerequisites fit into workflows: - Sales process (with prepayment) - Sales process (without prepayment)

docs.title: Restock or produce
docs.text:
This tutorial explains, in simple terms, what to do when you get a sales order and don’t have enough stock before delivery.

  • You can buy more (resupply) — Order the missing goods from a supplier. Example: You sell pine tables and have 2 in stock but need 10. Create a Supply Order for 8 finished tables (or for wood, legs, screws if you assemble in‑house).
  • Or you can produce more (make) — Build the missing goods with your own process. Example: You manufacture pine tables from wood and hardware. Create a Production Order for 8 tables and consume the needed materials.

Note

Which option applies depends on your business model:

  • Trading company (buy/sell finished goods) → usually Buy
  • Manufacturer (you make the goods) → usually Produce (and buy raw materials if missing)
  • Services/software → usually neither (no stock to move)

Tip

Before you start: ensure Processes, Inputs, and Outputs are defined.

docs.title: 1. Detect shortage
docs.text:
• Go to the published Sales Order and review ordered items, then open Stock to check current balances per warehouse/location.
  • When creating an Issue document, for example, via Linked Documents → + Full Issue. If stock is insufficient, the system shows a warning and prevents you from continuing or publishing until quantities are available.
  • In production, open Requirements to see which materials or semi‑products are short for planned operations.

docs.title: 2. Decide: Resupply or Produce
docs.text:
• If you buy/sell finished goods → proceed with Resupply.
  • If you manufacture goods → proceed with Produce (and Resupply raw materials/semi products as needed).

docs.title: 3.1 (Optional) Send an Inquiry
docs.text:
1. Go to Supply / Documents / Inquiries.
  2. Use the action button to create a draft inquiry.
  3. Add items, request price and lead time; Click Publish to confirm the inquiry.

docs.title: 3.2 Create a Supply Order
docs.text:
• From the Inquiry (or directly), open Linked Documents → + Supply Order.
  • Confirm supplier, items, and delivery date; Click Publish.

docs.title: 3.3 Receive into stock
docs.text:
1. In the Supply Order, open Linked Documents → + Receive.
  2. Select Warehouse and Locations, confirm received quantities; Click Publish.
  3. (Optional) Verify balances in Stock or Stock View by Location.

Note

In a normal supply chain process, after goods are received, the supplier’s Received invoice must be recorded and settled through a Payment Order in the Accounting domain. These financial steps are documented separately.

docs.title: 4. Produce (make)
docs.text:
Important

Ensure your process/operations exist in Processes with defined Inputs/Outputs.

docs.title: 4.1 Create a production order
docs.text:
1. Go to Production / Production Orders
  2. Use the action button to create a draft production order
  3. Select Product, Process, Quantity, Due date, Organization unit; Click Publish to commit
  4. Set Status to Active to make the order available in Execution

Tip

For more information on creating production orders, see How to create a new production order.

docs.title: 4.2 Resolve any input shortages
docs.text:
1. Open Requirements.
  2. Use the filter Show planned operations to see missing materials/semi-products for the production order.
  3. For short inputs, use the + sign top create a new Supply order and complete the Receive step (see 3.3).

docs.title: 4.3 Record execution
docs.text:
Use the Execution module to track production progress:

  1. Enter produced items via the Produce button.
  2. Access the activity selection menu using the action button to record:
    • Consumed — materials used during production
    • Effort — labor time spent
    • Loss — quantity scrapped and the reason (if any)
    • Downtime — equipment stops and duration (if any)
  3. When the order is complete, click on the Stop button to finalize it.

docs.title: 5. Continue the sales flow
docs.text:
• Return to the Sales Order and follow the delivery/invoicing tutorials:
  • Sales process (with prepayment)
  • Sales process (without prepayment)

Tip

After completion, you can review any details in the list of closed Production orders.

docs.title: Sales process (with prepayment)
docs.text:
This guide walks through a typical sales process including a prepayment step. Use links for details; do not duplicate configuration here.

flowchart LR
  OF[Offer] --> PI[Proforma invoice] --> PR[Prepayment] --> SO[Sales order] --> DN["Delivery note<br>+ Issue"] --> II[Issued invoice] --> PA[Payments]

Tip

Follow this guide step‑by‑step to configure the platform. Use the links to open each code list or setting if you need further details, then return to this page to continue with the next step.

Note

Inventory movement occurs at Issue. Prepayment and Issued invoice record financial transactions.

docs.title: 1. Create and publish a sales offer
docs.text:
Create a commercial offer to confirm prices, quantities, and validity with the customer.

  1. Go to Sales / Documents / Offers.
  2. Use the action button to create a draft offer.
  3. Fill Customer, Expiration date, and add items in the Details section.
  4. Fill any optional fields as needed.
  5. Click Publish to confirm the document.

docs.title: 2. Create a proforma invoice
docs.text:
Turn the agreed offer into a proforma to request an advance and share payment details.

  1. From the committed offer, use Linked documents → + Proforma invoice.

  1. Adjust Reference type, Organization bank account, Validity date, and any other optional fields as needed.
  2. Adjust product quantities according to how much the customer has agreed to pay in advance. Click a product line to open its edit section and set the quantity that will be prepaid; totals update accordingly.

  1. Click Publish.

docs.title: 3. Record a prepayment (partial or full)
docs.text:
Record the customer’s advance so the order is financially covered before delivery.

  1. From the committed proforma invoice, use Linked documents → + Prepayment.

  1. Fill:
    1. Due date
    2. Reference type/number
    3. Organization bank account
    4. Payment method
  2. Review that prepayment lines and amounts match the proforma quantities set in Step 2 - Create a proforma invoice.
  3. Click Publish to commit the prepayment.

docs.title: 4. Create a sales order
docs.text:
Create a sales order to reserve stock and plan fulfillment.

  1. Go back to the previously committed offer, and use Linked documents → + Sales order.

  1. Confirm quantities and delivery details and click Publish.

docs.title: 4a. Restock or produce (if needed)
docs.text:
If items are unavailable, see Restock or produce for options to procure or manufacture before delivery.

For production companies, a quick way to create a production order is from the published sales order: - Linked documents → + Production order

This creates a Production order draft that can be committed later in the Production domain.

docs.title: 5. Deliver goods
docs.text:
The sales order is ready; prepare the shipment and move stock out of the warehouse.

Follow these operational steps to move stock out of the warehouse:

  1. From the sales order, open Linked documents → + Delivery note. Verify customer, delivery address, and add the items to be shipped. You can adjust quantities if only part of the order is being delivered.
  2. In the delivery note, open Linked documents → + Full issue.

Select the warehouse and location(s), confirm quantities to pick. 3. Click Publish to commit the issue. This moves stock out of our warehouse and updates inventory balances. 4. (Optional) Verify the change in Stock view by location.

docs.title: 6. Issue the final invoice and apply prepayment
docs.text:
Issue the final invoice for delivered goods, apply the prepayment, and collect any balance.

  1. From the delivery note or the sales order, open Linked documents → + Issued invoice.
  2. Link the previously recorded prepayment via Linked documents → Prepayment to reduce the due amount.

  1. Review the final totals and add Payment methods if needed.
  2. Click Publish and record remaining payments via the Payment button to complete the transaction.

Tip

  • Use Linked documents to step through each stage and confirm auto-filled data (customer, items).
  • Open Company cards to review customer history, orders, and balances.

docs.title: Sales process (without prepayment)
docs.text:
This guide walks through a typical sales process without using prepayments. Use links for details; do not duplicate configuration here.

flowchart LR
  OF[Offer] --> SO[Sales order] --> DN["Delivery note<br>+ Issue"] --> II[Issued invoice] --> PA[Payments]

Tip

Follow this guide step‑by‑step to configure the platform. Use the links to open each code list or setting if you need further details, then return to this page to continue with the next step.

Note

  • In some use cases the process starts directly with a Sales Order. The Offer step is optional.
  • Inventory movement occurs at Issue.
  • Issued Invoice records revenue and payments.

docs.title: 1. Create and publish a sales offer (optional)
docs.text:
Create a commercial offer to confirm prices, quantities, and validity with the customer.

  1. Go to Sales / Documents / Offers.
  2. Use the action button to create a draft sales offer.
  3. Fill Customer, Expiration date, and add items in the Details section.
  4. Click Publish to confirm the document.

docs.title: 2. Create a sales order
docs.text:
Create a sales order to reserve stock and plan fulfillment.

  1. From the committed offer, use Linked documents → + Sales order.

  1. Confirm quantities and delivery details, then click Publish.

docs.title: 2a. Restock or produce (if needed)
docs.text:
If items are unavailable, see Restock or produce for options to procure or manufacture before delivery.

For production companies, a quick way to create a production order is from the published sales order: - Linked documents → + Production order.

This creates a Production order draft that can be committed later in the Production domain.

docs.title: 3. Deliver goods
docs.text:
The sales order is ready; prepare the shipment and move stock out of the warehouse.

  1. From the sales order, open Linked documents → + Delivery note. Verify Customer, Delivery address, and add the items to be shipped. You can adjust quantities if only part of the order is being delivered.
  2. In the delivery note, open Linked documents → + Full issue.

Select the Warehouse and Location(s), confirm quantities to pick. 3. Click Publish to commit the issue. This moves stock out and updates inventory balances. 4. (Optional) Verify the change in Stock view by location.

docs.title: 4. Issue the final invoice and record payments
docs.text:
Invoice delivered goods and record payment(s).

  1. From the sales order or the delivery note, open Linked documents → + Issued invoice.
  2. Review the final totals and add Payment methods if needed.
  3. Click Publish.
  4. Record incoming payments (partial or full) via the Payment button.

Tip

  • Use Linked documents to step through each stage and confirm auto-filled data (customer, items).
  • Open Company cards to review customer history, orders, and balances.

docs.title: Two-factor authentication
docs.text:
Two-factor authentication (2FA) provides an additional layer of security when signing in to the platform.

When enabled, the system sends a temporary authentication code to the user’s email address. The user must enter this code to complete the sign-in process.

Important

Two-factor authentication works only if:

  • the functionality is enabled on the platform
  • the user has a valid email address configured in System / Users

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The validity period of the authentication code can be configured in:

System / Configuration / Identity / Email 2FA

The setting defines how long (in seconds) the authentication code remains valid before it expires.

docs.title: Authentication process
docs.text:
1. Enter your username and password.
  2. The system sends an authentication code to your email address.
  3. Open the email and copy the received code.
  4. Paste the code into the authentication screen.
  5. After successful verification, access to the platform is granted.

docs.title: Domene
docs.text:
Poslovne funkcionalnosti u Tom PIT.Connected organizirane su u domene.

Domena objedinjuje sve funkcionalnosti vezane uz određeno poslovno područje, uključujući:

  • Dokumente i transakcije
  • Prikaze i izvješća
  • Upravljanje i konfiguraciju
  • Glavne podatke i šifrarnike

Ako ste novi na platformi, počnite odabirom domene koja najbolje odgovara vašem poslovnom procesu. Također možete upotrijebiti polje za pretraživanje kako biste brzo pronašli određene dokumente, postavke ili pojmove.
